title.zh: 卷一百八十六 列傳第七十三: 張楨 歸暘 陳祖仁 成遵 曹鑑 張翥
title.en: Volume 186 Biographies 73: Zhang Zhen, Gui Yang, Chen Zuren, Cheng Zun, Cao Jian, Zhang Zhu
title.raw: 卷一百八十六 列傳第七十三: 張楨 歸暘 陳祖仁 成遵 曹鑑 張翥 Volume 186 Biographies 73: Zhang Zhen, Gui Yang, Chen Zuren, Cheng Zun, Cao Jian, Zhang Zhu

sentences.zh: 張楨字約中，汴人。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhen, courtesy name Yuezhong, was a man of Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhen, style name Yuezhong, was a native of Bian (Kaifeng).

sentences.zh: 幼刻苦讀書，登元統元年進士第，授彰德路錄事，辟河南行省掾。

translations.literal: From youth he read books with bitter effort; he passed the jinshi examination in the first year of Yuantong, was appointed recorder of Zhangde Circuit, and was recruited as a clerk of the Henan Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He studied diligently from childhood, passed the jinshi in Yuantong 1, was made recorder of Zhangde Circuit, and joined the Henan Branch Secretariat as a clerk.

sentences.zh: 楨初娶祁氏，祁生貴富家，頗驕縱，見楨貧，不為禮，合卺踰月，即出之。

translations.literal: Zhen first married the Qi clan; Qi was born to a wealthy noble family, quite proud and unrestrained; seeing Zhen poor, she showed no courtesy; after the wedding cup passed a month, he divorced her.
translations.idiomatic: His first wife was of the Qi clan, from a rich and pampered family who treated the poor Zhen with disdain; within a month of their wedding he sent her away.

sentences.zh: 祁之兄訟于官，且污楨以黯昧事，左右司官聽之，楨因移疾不出，滯案俱積。

translations.literal: Qi's elder brother sued at court and moreover slandered Zhen with a shady affair; the Left and Right Department officials heard the case; Zhen therefore pleaded illness and did not go out; stalled cases all piled up.
translations.idiomatic: Her brother sued in court and accused Zhen of misconduct. While the Left and Right Department officials heard the case, Zhen pleaded illness and stayed home, and all pending matters stagnated.

sentences.zh: 平章政事月魯帖木兒怒曰：「張楨，剛介士也，豈汝曹所當議耶！」

translations.literal: Grand Councillor Yuelu Temur said angrily: "Zhang Zhen is a stern and upright gentleman—are you lot fit to discuss him!"
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councillor Yuelu Temur raged: "Zhang Zhen is a man of firm integrity—who are you to judge him!"

sentences.zh: 郎中虎者禿謁而謝之，乃起。

translations.literal: Bureau Director Huzhe Tu went to visit and apologize to him, and only then did Zhen resume his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Bureau Director Huzhe Tu came to apologize, and only then did Zhen return to office.

sentences.zh: 范孟為亂，矯殺月魯帖木兒等，城中大擾，楨暮夜縋城出，得免。

translations.literal: Fan Meng made rebellion and falsely killed Yuelu Temur and others; the city was greatly disturbed; at night Zhen let himself down from the wall by rope and escaped, narrowly surviving.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Meng rebelled and murdered Yuelu Temur and others under forged orders, the city fell into chaos; Zhen lowered himself from the wall by rope at night and escaped.

sentences.zh: 逾年，除高郵縣尹，門無私謁。

translations.literal: After a year, he was appointed magistrate of Gaoyou County, and no one paid private calls at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was made magistrate of Gaoyou County, and his door saw no private solicitations.

sentences.zh: 縣民張提領，尚任俠，武斷鄉曲。

translations.literal: A county resident named Zhang the Provision Leader still valued chivalric daring and tyrannized the countryside.
translations.idiomatic: Among the county people, one Zhang the Provision Leader still lived by the code of the knight-errant and bullied his neighbors at will.

sentences.zh: 一日，至縣有所囑，楨執之，盡得其罪狀，里中受其抑者，咸來訴焉，乃杖而徒之，人以為快。

translations.literal: One day he came to the county seat to press a request; Zhen seized him and fully established his crimes; those in the hamlets whom he had oppressed all came to lodge complaints, whereupon Zhen had him beaten and banished, and people rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: One day he came to the yamen with a favor to ask; Zhen arrested him, uncovered every count of his guilt, and when all who had suffered his oppression in the countryside came forward to accuse him, Zhen had him flogged and exiled—to general satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 守城千戶狗兒妻崔氏，為其小婦所譖，虐死，其鬼憑七歲女詣縣訴楨，備言死狀，屍見瘞舍後。

translations.literal: Cui, wife of Gou'er, a garrison commander of a thousand households, was slandered by his junior wife, tortured to death; her ghost possessed a seven-year-old girl and went to the county to accuse Zhen, stating in full how she had died, and the corpse was found buried behind the lodging house.
translations.idiomatic: Cui, wife of Gou'er, a city-garrison commander of a thousand households, was framed by his concubine, abused, and killed; her spirit entered a seven-year-old girl who came to the county yamen to plead before Zhen, recounting every detail of her death, and the body was found where it had been secretly buried behind the quarters.

sentences.zh: 楨率吏卒即其所，發土得屍，拘狗兒及小婦，鞫之，皆伏辜，人以為神明焉。

translations.literal: Zhen led clerks and soldiers to the spot, dug up the earth and obtained the corpse, detained Gou'er and the junior wife, interrogated them, and both confessed their guilt; people regarded him as divine.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen led clerks and constables straight to the place, exhumed the corpse, seized Gou'er and the concubine, and examined them until both admitted guilt; the people took him for something more than human.

sentences.zh: 累除中政院判官，至正八年，拜監察御史，劾太尉阿乞剌欺罔之罪，並言：「明里董阿、也裡牙、月魯不花，皆陛下不共戴天之仇，伯顏賊殺宗室嘉王、郯王一十二口，稽之古法，當伏門誅，而其子兄弟尚仕於朝，宜急誅竄。

translations.literal: After successive appointments he became vice-director of the Central Secretariat for Palace Affairs; in the eighth year of Zhizheng he was made investigating censor and impeached Grand Preceptor Aqila for deceit, also stating: 'Mingli Dong'a, Yeliya, and Yuelu Buhua are all enemies with whom Your Majesty cannot live under the same sky; Bayan murdered twelve members of the imperial clan, the Princes Jia and Tan— by ancient law they should suffer execution at the gate, yet their sons and brothers still hold office at court and should swiftly be put to death and banished.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through several posts to vice-director of the Central Secretariat for Palace Affairs; in Zhizheng 8 he was appointed investigating censor and charged Grand Preceptor Aqila with fraud, adding: 'Mingli Dong'a, Yeliya, and Yuelu Buhua are mortal foes of Your Majesty; Bayan butchered twelve kinsmen of the imperial house, the Princes Jia and Tan—for which ancient law demands death at the palace gate—yet their sons and brothers still serve at court and ought to be executed and driven out at once.

sentences.zh: 別兒怯不花阿附權奸，亦宜遠貶。

translations.literal: Berkebua, who fawned on powerful traitors, should also be banished far away.
translations.idiomatic: Berkebua, who had curried favor with the powerful and corrupt, should likewise be sent into distant exile.

sentences.zh: 今災異迭見，盜賊蜂起，海寇敢於要君，閫帥敢於玩寇，若不振舉，恐有唐末籓鎮噬臍之禍。」

translations.literal: Now omens and prodigies appear in succession, bandits swarm forth, sea raiders dare to hold the sovereign to ransom, and frontier commanders dare to toy with the enemy; if no vigorous measures are taken, I fear the calamity of late Tang when regional warlords devoured one another.'
translations.idiomatic: Portents and rebellions now come one after another; pirates at sea dare extort the throne, and border generals dare trifle with the foe. Unless the court rouses itself, we may see the late-Tang disaster of warlords tearing the realm apart from within.'

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: His words were not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The throne would not listen.

sentences.zh: 及毛貴陷山東，上疏陳十禍，根本之禍有六，征討之禍有四，歷數其弊：一曰輕大臣，二曰解權綱，三曰事安逸，四曰杜言路，五曰離人心，六曰濫刑獄，所謂根本之禍六也。

translations.literal: When Mao Gui overran Shandong, he submitted a memorial setting forth ten calamities: six fundamental calamities and four calamities of campaigning, enumerating the abuses: first, slighting great ministers; second, loosening the bonds of authority; third, pursuing ease; fourth, blocking the path of remonstrance; fifth, alienating hearts; sixth, abusing prisons—these being the six called fundamental calamities.
translations.idiomatic: When Mao Gui seized Shandong, he memorialized the throne on ten disasters—six rooted in government itself and four in the conduct of war—listing the abuses: treating great ministers lightly; letting the reins of power slip; settling into comfort; shutting the road of candid speech; estranging the people's hearts; and filling the prisons without cause. These were the six fundamental ills he named.

sentences.zh: 其言事安逸之禍，略曰：「臣伏見陛下以盛年入纂大統，履艱難而登大寶，因循治安，不預防慮，寬仁恭儉，漸不如初。

translations.literal: On the calamity of pursuing ease he wrote in summary: 'Your servant has observed that Your Majesty in the prime of life succeeded to the great succession, treading hardship to ascend the great treasure, yet followed along in mere peace and order without preventive forethought; your generous kindness and respectful frugality have gradually fallen short of what they were at first.
translations.idiomatic: On the evil of ease he wrote in part: 'I have seen Your Majesty, still in your prime, take up the great succession after hardship and win the throne—yet drift along in complacent peace without looking ahead; the generous restraint you showed at first has slowly worn away.

sentences.zh: 今天下可謂多事矣，海內可謂不寧矣，天道可謂變常矣，民情可謂難保矣，是陛下警省之時，戰兢惕厲之日也。

translations.literal: Now the realm may be called beset with troubles, within the seas may be called unsettled, the way of Heaven may be called changed from the norm, and the people's hearts may be called hard to secure—this is the time for Your Majesty to be vigilant and the day to stand in awe and exert caution.
translations.idiomatic: The empire is in turmoil, the realm is not at rest, Heaven's signs are erratic, and the people's loyalty cannot be relied on. This is the hour for vigilance and the day for trembling care.

sentences.zh: 陛下宜臥薪嘗膽，奮發悔過，思祖宗創業之難，而今日墜亡之易，於是而修實德，則可以答天意，推至誠，則可以回人心。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should sleep on brushwood and taste gall, rouse yourself to repent, reflect on the difficulty with which the ancestors founded the enterprise and how easily it may fall today; thereby cultivate real virtue and you may answer Heaven's intent; extend utmost sincerity and you may turn back the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: You should brace yourself as King Goujian did, repent in earnest, remember how hard the founders labored and how easily the house may fall now; cultivate true virtue to answer Heaven, and show utmost sincerity to win the people back.

sentences.zh: 凡土木之勞，聲色之好，燕安鴆毒之戒，皆宜痛撤勇改。

translations.literal: All labors of earth and timber, fondness for sound and beauty, and the warning of ease and poisoned wine should be painfully swept away and boldly reformed.
translations.idiomatic: Every palace building project, every indulgence in music and women, every taste of the poisoned cup of complacency—you should cut them off resolutely and reform at once.

sentences.zh: 有不盡者，亦宜防微杜漸，而禁於未然，黜宮女，節浮費，畏天卹人。

translations.literal: Where anything remains incomplete, you should also guard against the subtle and stop the gradual, forbidding it before it arises: dismiss palace women, curtail extravagant expenditure, fear Heaven and pity the people.
translations.idiomatic: Where you cannot finish the purge, you should still check evil at its root and forbid it before it grows: dismiss superfluous palace women, cut wasteful spending, fear Heaven, and care for the people.

sentences.zh: 而陛下乃安焉處之，如天下太平無事時，此所謂根本之禍也。」

translations.literal: Yet Your Majesty rests at ease in it as though the realm were at great peace with nothing amiss—this is what is called a fundamental calamity.'
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your Majesty sits at ease as if the world were at peace. That is the fundamental calamity I mean.'

sentences.zh: 至若不慎調度，不資群策，不明賞罰，不擇將帥，所謂征討之禍四也。

translations.literal: As for not carefully regulating supplies, not relying on collective counsel, not clarifying rewards and punishments, and not choosing generals and commanders—these are called the four calamities of campaigning.
translations.idiomatic: As for careless logistics, refusal to heed collective counsel, muddled rewards and punishments, and the failure to choose the right commanders—these are the four war-related ills.

sentences.zh: 其言不明賞罰之禍，略曰：「臣伏見調兵六年，初無紀律之法，又無激勸之宜，將帥因敗為功，指虛為實，大小相謾，上下相依，其性情不一，而邀功求賞則同。

translations.literal: On the calamity of unclear rewards and punishments he wrote in summary: 'Your servant has observed that troops have been mobilized for six years with no laws of discipline at the outset and no measures to encourage and spur them on; commanders turn defeat into merit and call the empty real; great and small deceive one another and high and low rely on each other—their temperaments are not one, yet in claiming merit and seeking reward they are the same.
translations.idiomatic: On confused rewards and punishments he wrote: 'For six years the armies have been mobilized without real discipline and without incentives that work. Generals turn defeat into victory on paper, call phantoms facts, lie to one another up and down the chain—different in character, alike in hunting rewards.

sentences.zh: 是以有覆軍之將，殘民之將，怯懦之將，貪婪之將，曾無懲戒，所經之處，雞犬一空，貨財俱盡。

translations.literal: Hence there are generals who destroy their armies, generals who ruin the people, cowardly generals, and greedy generals, yet never any punishment; wherever they pass, fowl and dogs are swept clean away and goods and wealth are utterly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: So we have commanders who lose whole armies, who ravage the people, who are cowards, who are thieves—and none are punished. Wherever they march, not a chicken or dog is left, and every store of goods is stripped bare.

sentences.zh: 及其面諛遊說，反以克復受賞。

translations.literal: When they come forward to flatter and lobby, they are instead rewarded for having recovered territory.
translations.idiomatic: Then they come to court with smooth words and are rewarded for reconquest.

sentences.zh: 今克復之地，悉為荒墟，河南提封三千餘里，郡縣星羅棋布，歲輸錢穀數百萬計，而今所存者，封丘、延津、登封、偃師三四縣而已。

translations.literal: The territories now said to be recovered are all wasteland; the Henan commandery extends over more than three thousand li, its counties and districts scattered like stars in a chessboard, yearly delivering grain and money in sums of millions—yet what survive today are only Fengqiu, Yanjin, Dengfeng, and Yanshi, three or four counties.
translations.idiomatic: The land they claim to have recovered is ruin. Henan alone spans more than three thousand li, its counties once thick as stars on a board, paying millions in grain and cash each year—yet only Fengqiu, Yanjin, Dengfeng, and Yanshi, three or four counties, still stand.

sentences.zh: 兩淮之北，大河之南，所在蕭條。

translations.literal: North of the two Huai rivers and south of the Great River, wherever one looks there is desolation.
translations.idiomatic: North of the Huai and south of the Yellow River, desolation is everywhere.

sentences.zh: 夫有土有人有財，然後可望軍旅不乏，饋餉不竭。

translations.literal: Only when there is land, people, and wealth may one hope that armies will not lack men and supplies will not run dry.
translations.idiomatic: Only with land, people, and wealth can armies be kept full and supplies unbroken.

sentences.zh: 今寇敵已至之境，固不忍言，未至之處​​，尤可寒心，如此而望軍旅不乏，饋餉不竭，使天雨粟，地湧金，朝夕存亡且不能保，況以地方有限之費，而供將帥無窮之欲哉！

translations.literal: The regions where bandits and enemies have already arrived are too painful to speak of; the regions not yet reached are especially chilling to the heart. Yet in such circumstances to hope that armies will not lack men and supplies will not run dry—even if Heaven rained grain and the earth spewed gold, survival from morning to evening could not be secured, how much less to meet the boundless desires of commanders with the limited resources of the regions!
translations.idiomatic: Where the enemy has already come, I can hardly bear to describe it; where he has not yet come, the prospect is worse still. Yet you still expect full armies and endless supplies—as if grain fell from Heaven and gold welled from the earth—when day to day survival is in doubt. How can the empire's thin purse satisfy commanders' bottomless greed?

sentences.zh: 其為自啟亂階，亦已危矣。

translations.literal: That this opens the ladder of disorder by one's own hand is already perilous.
translations.idiomatic: To open the door to chaos yourself is already a grave danger.

sentences.zh: 陛下事佛求福，飯僧消禍，以天壽節而禁屠宰，皆虛名也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty serves the Buddha to seek blessing, feeds monks to dispel calamity, and on the Heavenly Longevity Festival forbids slaughter—all empty names.
translations.idiomatic: You serve the Buddha for merit, feed monks to avert disaster, and ban slaughter on the Heavenly Longevity Festival—all empty gestures.

sentences.zh: 今天下殺人矣，陛下泰然不理，而曰吾將以是求福，福何自而至哉？

translations.literal: Now the realm is killing people, yet Your Majesty sits at ease and pays no heed, saying you will seek blessing thereby—whence should blessing come?
translations.idiomatic: Men are being killed across the empire while Your Majesty sits unmoved and says you will win blessing this way—from where should blessing come?

sentences.zh: 潁上之寇，始結白蓮，以佛法誘眾，終飾威權，以兵抗拒，視其所向，駸駸可畏，其勢不至於亡吾社稷、燼吾國家不已也。

translations.literal: The bandits of Yingshang first formed the White Lotus, used Buddhist teaching to entice the masses, and in the end arrayed authority and resisted with arms; seen in the direction they aim, they press forward fearsomely, and their momentum will not stop until they have destroyed our altars of soil and grain and burned our state to ashes.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels of Yingshang began with the White Lotus, lured crowds with Buddhist talk, then took up arms under a show of authority. The way they advance is terrifying; their momentum will not end until altar and state alike are ashes.

sentences.zh: 堂堂天朝，不思靖亂，而反為階亂，其禍至慘，其毒至深，其關係至大，有識者為之扼腕，有志者為之痛心，此征討之禍也。」

translations.literal: Our august celestial dynasty does not think to pacify disorder but instead provides steps to disorder; the calamity reaches the utmost in cruelty, the poison reaches the utmost in depth, and the connection reaches the utmost in magnitude—those with understanding wring their wrists over it, those with resolve ache at heart over it; this is a calamity of campaigning.'
translations.idiomatic: Our great dynasty does not seek to quell rebellion but supplies the steps to it. The harm is extreme, the poison deep, the stakes vast. Men of insight clench their fists; men of will ache in the heart. This is the war-related calamity.'

sentences.zh: 疏奏，不省。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted but not taken to heart.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went up; the court took no notice.

sentences.zh: 權臣惡其訐直。

translations.literal: Powerful ministers hated his blunt uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: The men in power hated his blunt honesty.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，除僉山南道肅政廉訪司事，至則劾中書參知政事也​​先不花、樞密院副使脫脫木兒、治書侍御史奴奴弄權誤國之罪，又不報。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was appointed commissioner of the Surveillance Commission for Shannan Circuit; on arrival he impeached Associate Administrator of the Secretariat Yexian Buhua, Vice Commissioner of the Privy Council Toto'er, and Investigating Censor Nunu for wielding power and misleading the state—again no response.
translations.idiomatic: In year 21 he was made commissioner of the Shannan surveillance circuit. On taking office he charged Yexian Buhua, associate administrator of the Secretariat, Toto'er, vice commissioner of the Privy Council, and Nunu, investigating censor, with abusing power and ruining the state. Again there was no answer.

sentences.zh: 方是時，孛羅帖木兒駐兵大同，察罕帖木兒駐兵洛陽，而毛貴據山東，勢逼京畿，二將玩寇不進，方以爭晉、冀為事，構兵相攻，互有勝負。

translations.literal: At this time Boluo Temur encamped his troops at Datong and Chaghan Temur at Luoyang, while Mao Gui held Shandong and his momentum pressed the capital region; the two generals toyed with the enemy and did not advance, being occupied with contesting Jin and Ji, raising arms against each other with alternating victories.
translations.idiomatic: Boluo Temur held Datong, Chaghan Temur Luoyang, while Mao Gui held Shandong and threatened the capital. The two generals dallied with the enemy and refused to advance, busy fighting each other over Shanxi and Hebei, trading victories.

sentences.zh: 朝廷乃遣也先不花、脫脫木兒、奴奴往解之，既受命，不前進。

translations.literal: The court then sent Yexian Buhua, Toto'er, and Nunu to mediate; once they had received the order, they did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Yexian Buhua, Toto'er, and Nunu to mediate—but once commissioned, they would not move.

sentences.zh: 楨又言其「貪懦庸鄙，苟懷自安之計，無憂國致身之忠。

translations.literal: Zhen again said of them: 'Greedy, cowardly, vulgar, and base, they harbor only plans for their own safety and have no loyalty of caring for the state and giving themselves to it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen wrote again that they were 'greedy, cowardly, vulgar men who cared only for their own safety and had no loyalty that would give the state their lives.

sentences.zh: 朝廷將使二家釋憾，協心討賊，此國之大事，謂宜風馳電走，而乃迂迴退懾，枉道延安以西，繞曲數千里，遲遲而行，使兩軍日夜仇殺，黎庶肝腦塗地，實此三人之所致也，宜急殛之，以救時危。」

translations.literal: The court wished the two houses to release their grudges and unite in heart to punish the bandits—this is a great matter of state and should be pursued like wind and lightning; yet they detour, shrink back in fear, go out of their way west of Yan'an, wind about for several thousand li, and travel slowly, so that the two armies day and night kill one another in hatred and the common people have their livers and brains smeared on the ground—this is truly brought about by these three men and they should swiftly be put to death to rescue the peril of the times.'
translations.idiomatic: The court meant them to reconcile the two factions and join against the rebels—a matter of state that demanded speed like wind and lightning. Instead they shrank back, detoured west of Yan'an, wandered thousands of li, and crawled along while the two armies butchered each other day and night and the people died in heaps. These three men caused it; put them to death at once to save the hour.'

sentences.zh: 亦不報。

translations.literal: Again no response.
translations.idiomatic: Again nothing was done.

sentences.zh: 楨乃慨然歎曰：「天下事不可為矣。」

translations.literal: Zhen then sighed with deep feeling: 'The affairs of the realm can no longer be undertaken.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhen sighed and said, 'Nothing under Heaven can be done anymore.'

sentences.zh: 即辭去，居河中安邑山谷間，結茅僅容膝。

translations.literal: He at once resigned and dwelt in the valleys of Anyi in Hezhong, building a thatched hut barely large enough to hold his knees.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned at once and lived in the valleys of Anyi in Hezhong, in a hut of thatch barely wide enough to kneel in.

sentences.zh: 有訪之者，不復言時事，但對之流涕而已。

translations.literal: When visitors came, he no longer spoke of current affairs but only wept before them.
translations.idiomatic: Visitors found him silent on public affairs; he could only weep in their presence.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，孛羅帖木兒犯闕，皇太子出居冀寧，奏除贊善，又除翰林學士，皆不起。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year Boluo Temur attacked the palace precincts; the heir apparent went out to dwell at Jining; Zhen was memorialized for appointment as tutor and again as Hanlin academician, but he did not take up either post.
translations.idiomatic: In year 24 Boluo Temur assaulted the capital; the heir apparent withdrew to Jining. Zhen was offered the posts of tutor and Hanlin academician but accepted neither.

sentences.zh: 擴廓帖木兒將輔皇太子入討孛羅帖木兒，遣使傳皇太子旨，賜以上尊，且訪時事，楨復書曰：「今燕趙齊魯之境，大河內外，長淮南北，悉為丘墟，關陝之區，所存無幾，江左日思薦食上國，湘漢荊楚川蜀，淫名僭號，幸我有變，利我多虞。

translations.literal: Kozha Temur was about to assist the heir apparent in entering to punish Boluo Temur; he sent an envoy bearing the heir apparent's command, bestowing superior wine and also inquiring about current affairs. Zhen replied in a letter: 'Now the regions of Yan, Zhao, Qi, and Lu, within and without the Great River, north and south of the long Huai, are all mounds and ruins; in the Guan and Shan region little survives; the lands south of the Yangtze daily think to feed on our state; in Xiang, Han, Jing, Chu, and the rivers and Shu of Sichuan, extravagant titles and usurped designations rejoice in our changes and profit from our many anxieties.
translations.idiomatic: Kozha Temur was about to assist the heir apparent in entering to punish Boluo Temur. He sent an envoy bearing the prince's command, bestowing fine wine and asking about current affairs. Zhen wrote back: 'Now the regions of Yan, Zhao, Qi, and Lu, the lands within and beyond the Yellow River and north and south of the long Huai, are all mounds and ruins. Of Guanzhong and Shaanxi little remains. Jiangzuo daily thinks to eat away at the upper state. In Xiang, Han, Jing, Chu, Sichuan, and Shu, those with licentious titles and usurped designations rejoice in our upheavals and profit from our many anxieties.

sentences.zh: 閣下國之右族，三世二王，得不思廉、藺之於趙，寇、賈之於漢乎？

translations.literal: Your Excellency is a great clan of the state, three generations and two kings—should you not think of Lian Po and Lin Xiangru toward Zhao, Kou Xun and Jia Yi toward Han?
translations.idiomatic: You are of the state's great houses, three generations and two kings ennobled—will you not remember Lian Po and Lin Xiangru for Zhao, Kou Xun and Jia Yi for Han?

sentences.zh: 京師一殘，假有不逞之徒，崛起草澤，借名義，尊君父，倡其說於天下，閣下將何以處之乎！

translations.literal: Once the capital is reduced to ruin, suppose some unbridled men rise from the marshes and meadows, borrow righteous names, honor ruler and father, and proclaim their doctrine to the realm—how will Your Excellency deal with them!
translations.idiomatic: Once the capital falls, some adventurer may rise from the wilds, take the name of loyalty to ruler and father, and preach his cause to the realm—what then will you do?

sentences.zh: 守京師者，能聚不能散，禦外侮者，能進不能退，紛紛籍籍，神分志奪，國家之事，能不為閣下憂乎！

translations.literal: Those who guard the capital can gather but cannot disperse; those who resist external insult can advance but cannot retreat—confused and clamorous, spirits divided and wills seized—can the affairs of state fail to be a worry for Your Excellency!
translations.idiomatic: Those who hold the capital can mass troops but not release them; those who face foreign foes can advance but not withdraw. Chaos divides mind and will. Can the state's affairs fail to trouble you?

sentences.zh: 《志》曰'不備不虞，不可以為師'，僕之惓惓為言者，獻忠之道也。

translations.literal: The Records say, 'Without preparation and without forethought one cannot command troops'—your servant's earnest words are the way of offering loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: The Records say: without preparation and foresight one cannot lead an army. My earnest words are loyalty offered in full.

sentences.zh: 然為言大要有三：保君父，一也；

translations.literal: Yet the great points of what is said are three: to preserve ruler and father is the first;
translations.idiomatic: Yet what I urge comes down to three things: first, preserve ruler and father;

sentences.zh: 扶社稷，二也；

translations.literal: to uphold the altars of soil and grain is the second;
translations.idiomatic: second, uphold the altars of state;

sentences.zh: 衛生靈，三也。

translations.literal: to guard the living people is the third.
translations.idiomatic: third, guard the living people.

sentences.zh: 請以近似者陳其一二：衛出公據國，至於不父其父；

translations.literal: Allow me to set forth one or two close parallels: Duke Chu of Wei held the state and came to the point of not treating his father as father;
translations.idiomatic: Let me cite near parallels: Duke Chu of Wei held the state and would not honor his father;

sentences.zh: 趙有沙丘之變，其臣成、兌平之，不可謂無功，而後至於不君其君；

translations.literal: Zhao had the turmoil at Sand Mound; its ministers Cheng and Dui pacified it—it cannot be said they had no merit—yet afterward they came to the point of not treating their lord as lord;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao had the Sand Mound crisis; Cheng and Dui quelled it—not without merit—yet afterward they would not treat their lord as lord;

sentences.zh: 唐肅宗流播之中，怵於邪謀，遂成靈武之纂。

translations.literal: Tang Suzong amid his wanderings, alarmed by wicked schemes, thereby brought about the usurpation at Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Suzong, adrift in exile, yielded to wicked counsel and accepted the usurpation at Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 千載之下，雖有智辯百出，不能為雪。

translations.literal: A thousand years below, though a hundred stratagems of wit and argument be deployed, it cannot be whitewashed.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand years on, no wit can wash that stain away.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 是豈可以不鑑之乎！

translations.literal: Can this fail to be taken as a mirror!
translations.idiomatic: Should this not be your mirror!

sentences.zh: 然吾聞之，天之所廢不驟也，驟其得志，肆其寵樂，使忘其覺悟之心，非安之也，厚其毒而降之罰也。

translations.literal: Yet I have heard that what Heaven discards is not sudden; when they swiftly gain their aim, indulge their favor and pleasure, and are made to forget the heart of awakening—that is not peace given them but heaping poison upon them and sending down punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I have heard that Heaven does not cast men down in a day. When the wicked rise fast, revel in favor, and forget conscience—that is not peace but poison heaped high before the fall.

sentences.zh: 天遂其欲，民厭其汰，而鬼神弗福也。

translations.literal: Heaven grants their desires, the people loathe their excess, and the ghosts and spirits do not bless them.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven grants their desires; the people hate their excess; the spirits withhold blessing.

sentences.zh: 其能久乎？

translations.literal: Can they long endure?
translations.idiomatic: Can they long endure?

sentences.zh: 閣下覽觀焉，謀出於萬全，則善矣。

translations.literal: Your Excellency should review and observe; if plans proceed from complete security, that is well.
translations.idiomatic: Read these cases, my lord, and plan for every contingency—that is best.

sentences.zh: 詢之輿議，急則其變不測，徐則其釁必起，通其往來之使，達其上下之情，得其情，則得其策矣。

translations.literal: Inquire of public opinion: if pressed urgently their changes are unpredictable; if delayed slowly their quarrel is sure to arise; open their coming and going envoys and penetrate the feelings of high and low—obtain their feelings and you obtain their strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Ask what the people say: press too hard and change comes unpredictably; move too slowly and quarrel is certain. Let envoys pass freely and learn what high and low feel—know that, and you know your policy.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：'君君臣臣父父子子。

translations.literal: Confucius said: 'Let the ruler be ruler, the minister minister, the father father, the son son.'
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said: 'Let the ruler act as ruler, the minister as minister, the father as father, and the son as son.'

sentences.zh: '今九重在上者如寄，青宮在下者如寄，生民之憂，國家之憂也，可不深思而熟計之哉！」

translations.literal: Now the ninefold gates above are like a lodging, the green palace below is like a lodging—the people's sorrow is the state's sorrow; can one fail to think deeply and plan carefully!'
translations.idiomatic: Today the throne above is like a guest-house, the heir apparent below like a guest-house—the people's grief is the state's grief. Should you not think long and plan hard!'

sentences.zh: 擴廓帖木兒深納其說，是用事克有成。

translations.literal: Kozha Temur deeply accepted his doctrine, and thereby the undertaking was able to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Kozha Temur took his counsel to heart, and the campaign succeeded.

sentences.zh: 後三年，卒。

translations.literal: Three years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he died.

sentences.zh: ○歸暘

translations.literal: ○ Gui Yang
translations.idiomatic: ○ Gui Yang

sentences.zh: 歸，暘字彥溫，汴梁人。

translations.literal: Gui, Yang styled Yanwen, was a man of Bianliang.
translations.idiomatic: Gui Yang, courtesy name Yanwen, was from Bianliang.

sentences.zh: 將生，其母楊氏夢朝日出東山上，有輕雲來掩之，故名暘。

translations.literal: When he was about to be born, his mother Lady Yang dreamed the morning sun rose on the eastern mountain and light clouds came to veil it, hence he was named Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Before his birth his mother Lady Yang dreamed the morning sun rose over the eastern hills and light clouds veiled it, so he was named Yang.

sentences.zh: 學無師傳，而精敏過人。

translations.literal: In study he had no transmitted teacher, yet his keen intelligence surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: He had no formal teacher, yet his quick mind surpassed others.

sentences.zh: 登至順元年進士第，授同知潁州事，鉏姦擊強，人不敢以年少易之。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the first year of Zhishun and was appointed associate prefect of Yingzhou; he rooted out the wicked and struck down the strong, and people did not dare treat him lightly for his youth.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi in Zhishun 1 and became associate prefect of Yingzhou, rooting out villains and crushing the powerful; none dared slight him for his youth.

sentences.zh: 山東鹽司遣奏差至潁，恃勢為不法，暘執以下獄。

translations.literal: The Shandong Salt Commission sent a memorial envoy to Ying; relying on his power he acted unlawfully, and Yang seized him and cast him into prison.
translations.idiomatic: The Shandong Salt Commission sent a memorial envoy to Ying who abused his authority; Yang arrested him and threw him in jail.

sentences.zh: 時州縣奉鹽司甚謹，頤指氣使，輒奔走之，暘獨不為屈。

translations.literal: At the time prefectures and counties served the Salt Commission very scrupulously, pointing chin and ordering by breath—they would at once run to obey—but Yang alone would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures and counties then groveled before the Salt Commission at a glance; Yang alone would not bend.

sentences.zh: 轉大都路儒學提舉，未上。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Confucian intendant of the Dadu Circuit but did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Confucian intendant of the Dadu Circuit but never reported.

sentences.zh: 至元五年十一月，杞縣人范孟謀不軌，詐為詔使，至河南省中，殺​​平章月魯帖木兒、左丞劫烈、廉訪使完者不花、總管撒里麻，召官屬及去位者，署而用之，以段輔為左丞，使暘北守黃河口。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fifth year of Zhiyuan, Fan Meng of Qi County plotted sedition, falsely posing as an imperial envoy; he reached the Henan provincial center and killed Grand Councillor Yuelu Temur, Left Administrator Jielie, Surveillance Commissioner Wanzhe Buhua, and Prefect Salima; he summoned officials in office and those who had left office, appointed and used them, made Duan Fu left administrator, and sent Yang north to guard the Yellow River mouth.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Zhiyuan 5, Fan Meng of Qi County rebelled, posing as an imperial envoy. At the Henan provincial seat he killed Grand Councillor Yuelu Temur, Left Administrator Jielie, Surveillance Commissioner Wanzhe Buhua, and Prefect Salima, then summoned officials active and retired, gave them posts, made Duan Fu left administrator, and ordered Yang north to guard the Yellow River mouth.

sentences.zh: 暘力拒不從，賊怒，係於獄，眾叵測所為，暘無懼色。

translations.literal: Yang strenuously refused and would not obey; the rebels were enraged and bound him in prison; the crowd could not fathom what he would do, yet Yang showed no fear.
translations.idiomatic: Yang refused outright. The rebels in rage threw him in prison; no one could guess what he would do, yet he showed no fear.

sentences.zh: 已而賊敗，污賊者皆獲罪，暘獨免。

translations.literal: Before long the rebels were defeated; those who had stained themselves with the rebels were all punished, but Yang alone was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the rebels fell; all who had served them were punished, but Yang alone went free.

sentences.zh: 同里有吳炳者，嘗以翰林待制徵，不起。

translations.literal: In the same hamlet was one Wu Bing, who had once been summoned as Hanlin awaiting edict but did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: A neighbor, Wu Bing, had been summoned as Hanlin awaiting edict but had refused office.

sentences.zh: 賊呼炳司卯酉歷，炳不敢辭。

translations.literal: The rebels called on Bing to manage the mao-you calendar, and Bing did not dare refuse.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels made Bing keep the calendar; he did not dare refuse.

sentences.zh: 時人為之語曰：「歸暘出角，吳炳無光。」

translations.literal: People of the time made a saying of it: 'Gui Yang shows his horn; Wu Bing has no light.'
translations.idiomatic: People said: 'Gui Yang shows his horn; Wu Bing has lost his shine.'

sentences.zh: 暘自此名譽赫然。

translations.literal: From this Yang's fame blazed forth.
translations.idiomatic: From that day Yang's fame blazed.

sentences.zh: 明年，轉國子博士，拜監察御史。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Erudite of the National University and appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he became Erudite of the National University and investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 及入謝，台臣奏曰：「此即河南抗賊者也。」

translations.literal: When he entered to give thanks, a censorate official reported: 'This is the one who resisted the rebels in Henan.'
translations.idiomatic: When he came to give thanks, a censorate official said, 'This is the man who resisted the rebels in Henan.'

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「好事卿宜數為之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'Good deeds— you gentlemen should often perform them.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, 'Such good deeds—you should often do them.'

sentences.zh: 賜以上尊。

translations.literal: He was granted superior wine.
translations.idiomatic: He was given fine wine.

sentences.zh: 已而辭官歸，養親汴上，親既歿，家食久之。

translations.literal: Before long he resigned office and returned, supporting his parents at Bian; after his parents died, he lived at home on salary for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: He soon resigned and went home to care for his parents at Bian; after they died he lived in retirement for many years.

sentences.zh: 至正五年，除僉河南廉訪司事，行部西京，以法繩趙王府官屬之貪暴者，王三遣使請，不為動。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhizheng he was appointed commissioner of the Henan Surveillance Commission; touring the department at the Western Capital, he bound by law the greedy and violent among the Prince of Zhao's household staff; the prince three times sent envoys to plead, but he was not moved.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 5 he became commissioner of the Henan surveillance circuit. On tour at the Western Capital he prosecuted greedy and violent men among the Prince of Zhao's staff; the prince sent envoys three times to intercede, but Yang would not budge.

sentences.zh: 宣寧縣有殺人者，蔓引數十人，一讞得其情，盡釋之。

translations.literal: In Xuanding County there was a murder case that implicated several tens of people; with one interrogation he obtained the truth and released them all.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuanding County a murder case had dragged in dozens; one examination uncovered the truth and he freed them all.

sentences.zh: 沁州民郭仲玉，為人所殺，有司以蒲察山兒當之，暘察其誣，踪跡得其殺人者，山兒遂不死。

translations.literal: A man of Qinzhou, Guo Zhongyu, was killed by someone; the authorities made Pucha Shan'er answer for it; Yang saw it was a false charge, traced the trail and obtained the real killer, and Shan'er thus did not die.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhongyu of Qinzhou was murdered; officials pinned it on Pucha Shan'er. Yang saw the frame-up, tracked the killer, and Shan'er was spared.

sentences.zh: 六年，轉僉淮東廉訪司事，改宣文閣監書博士，兼經筵譯文官。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to commissioner of the Huaidong Surveillance Commission, then changed to Doctor Overseer of Writings at the Xuanwen Pavilion, also serving as translation officer for the Classics Colloquium.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he became commissioner of the Huaidong surveillance circuit, then Doctor Overseer of Writings at the Xuanwen Pavilion and translator for the Classics Colloquium.

sentences.zh: 七年，遷右司都事。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was promoted to director of the Right Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he was made director of the Right Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 順江酋長樂孫求內附，請立宣撫司，及置郡縣一十三處，暘曰：「古人有言：鞭雖長，不及馬腹。

translations.literal: The chieftain of Shunjiang, Lesun, sought to submit inward and asked to establish a pacification commission and to set up thirteen prefectures and counties. Yang said: 'The ancients had a saying: though the whip be long, it does not reach the horse's belly.
translations.idiomatic: Lesun, chieftain of Shunjiang, sought to submit and asked for a pacification commission and thirteen new counties. Yang said, 'The ancients said: the whip may be long, but it cannot reach the horse's belly.

sentences.zh: 使郡縣果設，有事不救，則孤來附之意，救之，則罷中國而事外夷，所謂獲虛名而受實禍也。」

translations.literal: If prefectures and counties were really established, when trouble arose and we did not rescue them, we would betray the meaning of their coming to attach; if we rescued them, we would abandon the Middle Kingdom to serve outer barbarians—what is called gaining an empty name and receiving real calamity.'
translations.idiomatic: If we set up counties and then failed them in crisis, we betray those who came to us; if we rescued them, we would drain the heartland to serve border tribes—empty honor and real harm.'

sentences.zh: 與左丞呂思誠抗辨甚力。

translations.literal: He debated forcefully with Left Administrator Lü Sicheng.
translations.idiomatic: He argued fiercely with Left Administrator Lü Sicheng.

sentences.zh: 丞相太平笑曰：「歸都事善戇如此，何相抗乃爾邪！

translations.literal: Chief Councillor Taiping laughed and said: 'Director Gui is so good at being blunt—why resist each other so!
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councillor Taiping laughed and said, 'Director Gui is stubbornness itself—why fight each other so!

sentences.zh: 然其策果將焉出？」

translations.literal: Yet what policy will in fact come forth?'
translations.idiomatic: But what policy do you propose?'

sentences.zh: 暘曰：「其酋長可授宣撫，勿責其貢賦，使者賜以金帛，遣歸足矣。」

translations.literal: Yang said: 'Their chieftain may be granted pacification commissioner; do not demand their tribute and levies; let the envoy bestow gold and silks and send them back—that is enough.'
translations.idiomatic: Yang said, 'Make their chieftain a pacification commissioner, demand no tribute, give gold and silk through an envoy, and send them home—that is enough.'

sentences.zh: 卒從暘言。

translations.literal: In the end they followed Yang's words.
translations.idiomatic: In the end they took Yang's advice.

sentences.zh: 京師苦寒，有丐訴丞相馬前，丞相索皮服予之，仍核在官所藏皮服之數，悉給貧民。

translations.literal: The capital was bitterly cold; a beggar pleaded before the chief councillor's horse; the councillor sought fur garments and gave them to him, then checked the number of fur garments stored in official warehouses and gave them all to the poor.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was bitterly cold. A beggar pleaded before the chief councillor's horse; he took off his fur coat and gave it, then inventoried official fur stores and gave everything to the poor.

sentences.zh: 暘曰：「宰相當以廣濟天下為心，皮服能幾何，而欲給之邪！

translations.literal: Yang said: 'A chief councillor should take relieving the realm broadly as his heart—how many fur garments can there be, that you wish to supply them!
translations.idiomatic: Yang said, 'A chief councillor should seek to relieve the whole realm. How many furs can there be that you think to clothe everyone!

sentences.zh: 莫若錄寒飢者，稍賑之耳。」

translations.literal: Better to register those suffering cold and hunger and give them a little relief.'
translations.idiomatic: Better to register the cold and hungry and give modest relief.'

sentences.zh: 丞相悟而止。

translations.literal: The chief councillor understood and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The chief councillor took the point and stopped.

sentences.zh: 雲南死可伐叛，詔以元帥述律遵道往喻之；

translations.literal: Sikewafa of Yunnan rebelled; an edict ordered Marshal Shulü Zundao to go and instruct him;
translations.idiomatic: When Sikewafa rebelled in Yunnan, the court sent Marshal Shulü Zundao to reason with him;

sentences.zh: 未幾，命平章政事亦都渾將兵討之，事久無功。

translations.literal: Before long he ordered Grand Councillor Yiduhun to lead troops to punish him; the affair dragged on long without success.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Grand Councillor Yiduhun was sent with an army; the campaign dragged on without result.

sentences.zh: 二人上疏紛紜，中書欲罪述律，暘曰：「彼事未白，而專罪一人，豈法意乎？

translations.literal: The two men submitted tangled memorials; the Secretariat wished to punish Shulü; Yang said: 'The matter is not yet clear, yet you would punish one man alone—is that the intent of the law?
translations.idiomatic: Both filed conflicting memorials; the Secretariat wanted to punish Shulü. Yang said, 'The facts are unclear—how can you punish one man alone? That is not justice.

sentences.zh: 況一諭之而一討之，彼將何所適從？

translations.literal: Moreover, one moment instructing him and the next attacking him—what will they follow?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, you instruct them one day and attack the next—what are they to obey?

sentences.zh: 然亦非使者之罪也。」

translations.literal: Yet it is not the envoy's fault either.'
translations.idiomatic: Nor is it the envoy's fault.'

sentences.zh: 湖廣行省左丞沙班卒，其子沙的方為中書掾，請奔喪，丞相以沙的有兄弟，不許，暘曰：「孝者，人子之同情，以其有兄弟而沮其請，非所以孝治天下也。」

translations.literal: The Left Administrator of the Huguang Branch Secretariat, Shaban, died; his son Shadi was then a Secretariat clerk and asked leave to mourn; the chief councillor, because Shadi had brothers, did not permit it. Yang said: 'Filial piety is the common feeling of a son; to block his request because he has brothers is not how to govern the realm by filial piety.'
translations.idiomatic: When Shaban, left administrator of Huguang, died, his son Shadi, a Secretariat clerk, asked leave to mourn. The chief councillor refused because he had brothers. Yang said, 'Filial duty is every son's feeling; to deny him because he has brothers is not how to rule by filial example.'

sentences.zh: 遂從之。

translations.literal: They then followed his view.
translations.idiomatic: They granted the leave.

sentences.zh: 廣海ＯＤ賊入寇，詔朵兒只班將思播楊元帥軍以討之，暘曰：「易軍而將不諳教令，恐不能決勝。

translations.literal: Guanghai bandits invaded; an edict ordered Dorbanshar to lead the Sibao Yang Marshal's army to punish them. Yang said: 'To change the army while the commander does not know its orders and regulations—I fear victory cannot be decided.
translations.idiomatic: When Guanghai pirates raided, the court ordered Dorbanshar to lead Marshal Yang's Sibao army against them. Yang said, 'Swap the army and the new commander will not know its orders—you may not win.

sentences.zh: 若命楊就統其眾，彼悅於恩命，必能自效，所謂以夷狄攻夷狄，中國之利也。」

translations.literal: If Yang were ordered to take command of his own troops, they would rejoice at the grace of the appointment and surely exert themselves—what is called using barbarians to attack barbarians, the Middle Kingdom's advantage.'
translations.idiomatic: Let Yang keep command of his own men; they will welcome the favor and fight hard—using barbarians against barbarians, to the empire's profit.'

sentences.zh: 帝不從，後竟無功。

translations.literal: The emperor did not follow; in the end there was no success.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused; the campaign failed.

sentences.zh: 八年，升左司員外郎。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was promoted to vice director of the Left Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 he became vice director of the Left Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 中書用暘言，損河間餘鹽五萬引以裕民。

translations.literal: The Secretariat adopted Yang's words and reduced fifty thousand surplus salt quotas of Hejian to ease the people.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat took Yang's advice and cut fifty thousand Hejian salt quotas to ease the people.

sentences.zh: 楮幣壅不行，廷議出楮幣五百萬錠易銀實內藏，暘复持不可曰：「富商大賈，盡易其鈔於私家，小民何利哉！」

translations.literal: Paper currency was blocked and would not circulate; the court debated issuing five million ingots of paper notes to exchange for silver to fill the inner treasury. Yang again held it impossible and said: 'Great merchants and traders will all exchange their notes into private hands—what benefit for the common people!'
translations.idiomatic: Paper money would not circulate; the court proposed issuing five million ingots to swap for silver for the inner treasury. Yang again objected: 'Rich merchants will hoard the notes—what good is that for common folk?'

sentences.zh: 六月，遷參議樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he was transferred to deliberator of the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he became deliberator of the Privy Council.

sentences.zh: 時方國珍未附，詔江浙行省參知政事朵兒只班討之，一軍皆沒，而朵兒只班被執，將罪之，暘曰：「將之失利，其罪固當，然所部皆北方步騎，不習水戰，是驅之死地耳。

translations.literal: At the time Fang Guozhen had not submitted; an edict ordered Associate Administrator of the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat Dorbanshar to punish him; a whole army was lost and Dorbanshar was seized; they were about to punish him. Yang said: 'A general's defeat carries guilt—that is fitting; yet his troops were all northern infantry and cavalry, unpracticed in naval warfare—this was driving them to death.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Fang Guozhen had not yet submitted, and an edict ordered Dorjiban, Associate Administrator of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat, to punish him. His whole army was lost and Dorjiban was captured; the court was about to punish him. Yang said, 'A general's defeat certainly deserves blame, yet all the troops under him were northern infantry and cavalry, unpracticed in naval warfare. This was simply driving them into a place of death.

sentences.zh: 宜募海濱之民習水利者擒之。」

translations.literal: You should recruit coastal people skilled in water warfare to capture him.'
translations.idiomatic: Recruit coastal people who know naval warfare to take him.'

sentences.zh: 既而國珍遣人從朵兒只班走京師請降，暘曰：「國珍已敗我王師，又拘我王臣，力屈而來，非真降也。

translations.literal: Before long Guozhen sent men following Dorbanshar to the capital to request surrender. Yang said: 'Guozhen has already defeated our royal army and also detained our royal minister; coming when his strength is spent is not a true surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Guozhen sent men with Dorbanshar to the capital to sue for peace. Yang said, 'He has beaten our army and held our minister hostage—coming only when broken is not real surrender.

sentences.zh: 必討之以令四方。」

translations.literal: He must be punished to command the four quarters.'
translations.idiomatic: Punish him to show the realm.'

sentences.zh: 時朝廷方事姑息，卒從其請，後果屢叛，如暘言。

translations.literal: The court was then pursuing indulgence and in the end granted his request; afterward he rebelled repeatedly, as Yang had said.
translations.idiomatic: The court was in a conciliatory mood and granted his plea; he rebelled again and again, as Yang had warned.

sentences.zh: 遷御史臺都事，俄复參議樞密院事，十二月，升樞密院判官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to director of the Censorate; soon again deliberator of the Privy Council; in the twelfth month promoted to vice commissioner of the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: He became director of the Censorate, then again deliberator of the Privy Council; in the twelfth month he was made vice commissioner of the Privy Council.

sentences.zh: 九年正月，轉河西廉訪使，未上，改禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first month of the ninth year he was transferred to surveillance commissioner of Hexi but did not take office, and was changed to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 9 he was made surveillance commissioner of Hexi but never reported, then Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 會開端本堂，皇太子就學，召暘為贊善。

translations.literal: When the Duanyuan Hall was opened and the heir apparent began study, Yang was summoned as tutor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Duanyuan Hall opened for the heir apparent's studies, Yang was summoned as tutor.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷翰林直學士、同修國史，仍兼前職。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Hanlin academician and associate compiler of the national history, still holding his former post as well.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became Hanlin academician and associate compiler of the national history while keeping his tutor's post.

sentences.zh: 暘言：「師傅當與皇太子東西相向授書，其屬亦以次列坐，虛其中座，以待至尊臨幸，不然，則師道不立矣。」

translations.literal: Yang said: 'The master should face the heir apparent east and west to give the text; his subordinates should also sit in order, leaving the central seat empty to await the sovereign's visit—otherwise the way of the teacher cannot be established.'
translations.idiomatic: Yang said, 'The tutor and prince should face each other east and west to teach; attendants sit in order with the center seat left empty for the emperor's visit—otherwise teacher's authority is not established.'

sentences.zh: 時眾言人人殊，卒從暘議。

translations.literal: At the time every man's opinion differed; in the end they followed Yang's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Opinions differed; in the end they followed Yang.

sentences.zh: 俄以疾辭，帝遣左司郎中趙璉賜白金文綺，不受。

translations.literal: Soon he resigned on grounds of illness; the emperor sent Left Secretariat Director Zhao Lian to bestow white gold and patterned silks; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He soon resigned for illness; the emperor sent Zhao Lian of the Left Secretariat with white gold and brocade; he refused.

sentences.zh: 初，暘在上都時，脫脫自甘州還，且入相，中書參議趙期頤、員外郎李稷謁暘私第，致脫脫之命，屬草詔，暘辭曰：「丞相將為伊、周事業，入相之詔，當命詞臣視草，今屬筆於暘，恐累丞相之賢也。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yang was at Shangdu, Toghto returned from Ganzhou and was about to enter the chancellorship; Secretariat Deliberator Zhao Qiyi and Director Li Ji visited Yang's private residence conveying Toghto's command, entrusting him to draft the edict. Yang declined: 'The chief councillor will undertake the work of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou; the edict of entering the chancellorship should be ordered to literary officials to draft—now entrusting the brush to Yang, I fear it may burden the councillor's worth.'
translations.idiomatic: Earlier at Shangdu, Toghto returned from Ganzhou to take the chancellorship. Zhao Qiyi and Li Ji came to Yang's home with Toghto's order to draft the appointment edict. Yang declined: 'The councillor aims at the work of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou—such an edict should go to the academicians. Asking me would stain his reputation.'

sentences.zh: 期頤曰：「若帝命為之，奈何？」

translations.literal: Qiyi said: 'If the emperor commands it, what then?'
translations.idiomatic: Qiyi said, 'What if the emperor orders it?'

sentences.zh: 暘曰：「事理非順，亦當固辭。」

translations.literal: Yang said: 'If reason and circumstance are not fitting, one should still firmly decline.'
translations.idiomatic: Yang said, 'Even then one should refuse what is not right.'

sentences.zh: 期頤知不可屈，乃已。

translations.literal: Qiyi knew he could not be bent and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyi saw he could not be moved and gave up.

sentences.zh: 十年正月，遷四川行省參知政事，十二年，除刑部尚書，十五年，再除刑部尚書，凡三遷，皆以疾辭。

translations.literal: In the first month of the tenth year he was transferred to associate administrator of the Sichuan Branch Secretariat; in the twelfth year removed as Minister of Punishments; in the fifteenth year again removed as Minister of Punishments—in all three transfers he declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year's first month he became associate administrator of Sichuan; in year 12 Minister of Punishments; in year 15 again Minister of Punishments—three appointments, each declined for illness.

sentences.zh: 十七年，授集賢學士，兼國子祭酒，使者迫之，暘輿疾至京師，臥於南城不起。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was granted Academician of the Hall of Gathered Talents and concurrent Rector of the National University; envoys pressed him; Yang came by litter in illness to the capital and lay in the southern city unable to rise.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17 he was made Academician of the Hall of Gathered Talents and rector of the National University; envoys pressed him; Yang came by litter to the capital and lay ill in the southern quarter, unable to rise.

sentences.zh: 時海內多故，暘上三策：一曰振紀綱，二曰選將材，三曰審形勢。

translations.literal: The realm within the seas had many troubles; Yang submitted three policies: first, restore discipline and statutes; second, select generals of talent; third, examine the strategic situation.
translations.idiomatic: With turmoil across the realm, Yang offered three policies: restore law and order; choose able generals; read the strategic situation.

sentences.zh: 亹亹數千言，時以為老生常談，不能用。

translations.literal: Earnestly and at length several thousand words; people of the time took it as an old pedant's common talk and could not use it.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote thousands of earnest words; the court dismissed it as platitudes and did not act.

sentences.zh: 十一月，以集賢學士、資德大夫致仕，給半俸終身，辭不受。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he retired as Academician of the Hall of Gathered Talents and Grand Master of Cherished Virtue, granted half salary for life; he declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he retired with the titles Academician and Grand Master of Cherished Virtue, with half salary for life; he refused even that.

sentences.zh: 明年，乞骸骨，僑居弘州，徙蔚州，又徙宣德，皆間關避兵。

translations.literal: The next year he begged to return his bones, sojourned in Hongzhou, moved to Yuzhou, then moved to Xuande—all by hard paths avoiding warfare.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he asked to go home, lived in Hongzhou, moved to Yuzhou, then Xuande, each move a hard flight from war.

sentences.zh: 尋抵大同。

translations.literal: Soon he reached Datong.
translations.idiomatic: He soon reached Datong.

sentences.zh: 及關陝小寧，來居解之夏縣。

translations.literal: When Guan and Shan were slightly calm, he came to dwell at Xia County in Jie.
translations.idiomatic: When Guanzhong and Shaanxi grew quieter, he settled at Xia County in Jie Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 皇太子出冀寧，強起之，居數月，復還夏縣。

translations.literal: The heir apparent went out to Jining and forced him to rise; he dwelt several months, then returned again to Xia County.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir apparent withdrew to Jining he was pressed to serve; after some months he returned to Xia County.

sentences.zh: 二十七年卒，年六十三。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he died, aged sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year 27, aged sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 陳祖仁王遜志

translations.literal: Chen Zuren; Wang Xunzhi
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zuren; Wang Xunzhi

sentences.zh: 陳祖仁，字子山，汴人也。

translations.literal: Chen Zuren, styled Zishan, was a man of Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zuren, courtesy name Zishan, was from Bian.

sentences.zh: 其父安國，仕為常州晉陵尹。

translations.literal: His father Anguo served as magistrate of Jinling in Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Anguo served as magistrate of Jinling in Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖仁性嗜學，早從師南方，有文名。

translations.literal: Zuren by nature loved learning; he early followed teachers in the south and had a literary reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Zuren loved learning; he studied in the south from youth and won a name for letters.

sentences.zh: 至正元年，科舉復行，祖仁以《春秋》中河南鄉貢。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhizheng the civil examinations were restored; Zuren passed the Henan provincial recommendation with the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 1 examinations resumed; Zuren passed the Henan provincial test on the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 明年會試，在前列，及對策大廷，遂魁多士，賜進士及第，授翰林修撰、同知制誥，兼國史院編修官。

translations.literal: The next year in the metropolitan examination he was in the front rank; when he answered policy questions in the great court he came out first among the many scholars, was granted jinshi with honors, and appointed Hanlin compiler, associate director of edicts, and concurrent compiler of the National History Institute.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he ranked high in the metropolitan exam and topped the palace policy debate, taking jinshi with honors as Hanlin compiler, associate director of edicts, and compiler of the national history.

sentences.zh: 歷太廟署令、太常博士，遷翰林待制，出僉山東肅政廉訪司事，擢監察御史，復出為山北肅政廉訪司副使，召拜翰林直學士，升侍講學士，除參議中書省事。

translations.literal: He passed through Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, Erudite of the Imperial Sacrifices, was promoted to Hanlin awaiting edict, went out as commissioner of the Shandong Surveillance Commission, was elevated to investigating censor, again went out as vice commissioner of the Shanbei Surveillance Commission, was summoned as Hanlin academician, promoted to exposition academician, and removed as deliberator of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He served as director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and erudite of the Imperial Sacrifices, became Hanlin awaiting edict, commissioner of Shandong surveillance, investigating censor, vice commissioner of Shanbei surveillance, Hanlin academician, exposition academician, and Secretariat deliberator.

sentences.zh: 二十年五月，帝欲修上都宮闕，工役大興，祖仁上疏，其略曰：「自古人君，不幸遇艱虞多難之時，孰不欲奮發有為，成不世之功，以光復祖宗之業。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the twentieth year the emperor wished to repair the palaces at Shangdu and labor service was greatly raised; Zuren submitted a memorial, in summary: 'Since antiquity rulers, when unhappily meeting times of hardship and many difficulties, who did not wish to rouse themselves to achievement and accomplish an unworldly merit to restore and glorify the ancestors' enterprise?
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of year 20 the emperor planned to rebuild the Shangdu palaces and conscripted labor on a vast scale. Zuren memorialized in part: 'Since antiquity, which ruler in hard times has not wished to achieve something great and restore the founders' work?

sentences.zh: 苟或上不奉於天道，下不順於民心，緩急失宜，舉措未當，雖以此道持盈守成，猶或致亂，而況欲撥亂世反之正乎！

translations.literal: If above one does not follow Heaven's way and below one does not accord with the people's hearts, if urgency and ease miss their measure and measures are not fitting—even by this way to hold fullness and guard accomplishment one may still bring disorder, how much more to turn a chaotic age back to the right!
translations.idiomatic: If above you ignore Heaven's way and below lose the people's hearts, if timing and measures are wrong—even holding a full vessel you may bring ruin, let alone set a chaotic age right!

sentences.zh: 夫上都宮闕，創自先帝，修於累朝，自經兵火，焚毀殆盡，所不忍言，此陛下所為日夜痛心，所宜亟圖興復者也。

translations.literal: The palaces at Shangdu were founded by the former emperor and repaired through successive reigns; since passing through military fire they were burned nearly to nothing—what cannot bear to be spoken—this is what Your Majesty day and night grieves and what should urgently be planned for restoration.
translations.idiomatic: The Shangdu palaces were built by the founder and repaired by many reigns; war has burned them almost away—Your Majesty grieves day and night, and restoration is urgent.

sentences.zh: 然今四海未靖，瘡痍未瘳，倉庫告虛，財用將竭，乃欲驅疲民以供大役，廢其耕耨，而荒其田畝，何異扼其吭而奪之食，以速其斃乎！

translations.literal: Yet now the four seas are not pacified, wounds are not healed, storehouses report emptiness, revenues are about to be exhausted—yet you wish to drive the weary people to supply great labor, abandon their plowing and hoeing, and waste their fields—how is this different from clutching their throats and seizing their food to hasten their death!
translations.idiomatic: Yet the realm is not at peace, wounds are unhealed, treasuries empty, revenues failing—and you would drive exhausted people to great works, leave fields untilled and land waste. Is that not seizing their throats and their food to kill them faster?

sentences.zh: 陛下追惟祖宗宮闕，念茲在茲，然不思今日所當興復，乃有大於此者。

translations.literal: Your Majesty looks back to the ancestors' palaces and keeps them ever in mind, yet does not reflect that what should be restored today has something greater than this.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty thinks constantly of the ancestral palaces, yet what must be restored today is something greater than brick and timber.

sentences.zh: 假令上都宮闕未復，固無妨於陛下之寢處，使因是而違天道，失人心，或致大業之隳廢，則夫天下者亦祖宗之天下，生民者亦祖宗之生民，陛下亦安忍而輕棄之乎！

translations.literal: Suppose the Shangdu palaces were not restored—it would in no way hinder Your Majesty's sleeping quarters; but if because of this you violate Heaven's way, lose the people's hearts, or bring the great enterprise to ruin—then the realm is also the ancestors' realm and the living people are also the ancestors' living people—can Your Majesty bear to lightly abandon them!
translations.idiomatic: If Shangdu were never rebuilt, Your Majesty could still sleep in peace—but if this work makes you lose Heaven and the people and wreck the great enterprise, can you lightly abandon the ancestors' realm and people?

sentences.zh: 願陛下以生養民力為本，以恢復天下為務，信賞必罰，以驅策英雄，親正人，遠邪佞，以圖謀治道。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to take nourishing the people's strength as the root and recovering the realm as the task, to believe in rewards and sure punishments to drive heroes, to be close to upright men and distant from wicked flatterers, and to plan the way of good government.
translations.idiomatic: Take nourishing the people's strength as your root and recovering the realm as your task; reward and punish faithfully; draw heroes to you; keep upright men near and flatterers far; plan the way of good government.

sentences.zh: 夫如是，則承平之觀，不日咸复，詎止上都宮闕而已乎！」

translations.literal: If it is so, then the sight of enduring peace will in no long day all be restored—how would it stop at the Shangdu palaces alone!'
translations.idiomatic: Do that, and peace will return soon—not only at Shangdu!'

sentences.zh: 疏奏，帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted and the emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised the memorial and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 二十三年十二月，拜治書侍御史。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the twenty-third year he was appointed investigating censor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of year 23 he became investigating censor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時宦者資正使樸不花與宣政使橐驩，內恃皇太子，外結丞相搠思監，驕恣不法，監察御史傅公讓上章暴其過，忤皇太子意，左遷吐蕃宣慰司經歷。

translations.literal: At the time the eunuch Pacification Commissioner Puhua and the Xuanzheng Commissioner Tuo Huan, relying within on the heir apparent and linking without with Chief Councillor Toghto Temur, were arrogant and lawless. Investigating Censor Fu Gongrang submitted a memorial exposing their faults, offending the heir apparent's intent, and was demoted to administrator of the Tubo Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the eunuch Puhua, Zizheng Commissioner, and Toqon, Xuanzheng Commissioner, relied internally on the heir apparent and externally allied with Chief Councillor Shaosijian, acting with arrogant lawlessness. Investigating Censor Fu Gongrang submitted a memorial exposing their faults; because this offended the heir apparent, he was demoted to administrator of the Tubo Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 它御史連章論諫，皆外除。

translations.literal: Other censors submitted linked memorials of remonstrance; all were transferred outward.
translations.idiomatic: Other censors remonstrated in linked memorials; all were posted away from court.

sentences.zh: 祖仁上疏皇太子言：「御史糾劾橐驩、不花奸邪等事，此非御史之私言，乃天下之公論，台臣審問尤悉，故以上啟。

translations.literal: Zuren submitted a memorial to the heir apparent saying: 'The censors' impeachment of Tuo Huan, Buhua, and other wicked and depraved matters is not the censors' private speech but the public judgment of the realm; censorate officials examined and questioned with especial thoroughness, hence they reported upward.
translations.idiomatic: Zuren wrote the heir apparent: 'The censors' charges against Tuo Huan and Buhua are not private opinion but public judgment. The censorate examined the case thoroughly before reporting it.

sentences.zh: 今殿下未賜詳察，輒加沮抑，擯斥御史，詰責台臣，使奸臣蠹政之情，不得達於君父，則亦過矣。

translations.literal: Now Your Highness has not granted detailed examination but hastily added obstruction and suppression, driving out censors and reproaching censorate officials, so that the wicked ministers' corruption of government cannot reach ruler and father—that is also excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness has not looked into the matter but has blocked it, driven out the censors, and rebuked the censorate, so that wicked ministers' corruption cannot reach the emperor—that is going too far.

sentences.zh: 夫天下者祖宗之天下，臺諫者祖宗之所建立，以二豎之微，而於天下之重、臺諫之言，一切不恤，獨不念祖宗乎！

translations.literal: The realm is the ancestors' realm; the censorate and remonstrance offices are what the ancestors established—for two petty eunuchs to make you care nothing for the weight of the realm and the words of the censorate—do you alone not think of the ancestors!
translations.idiomatic: The realm is the ancestors' realm; the censorate is the ancestors' institution—for two eunuchs you ignore the realm's weight and the censors' words. Do you not remember the ancestors?

sentences.zh: 且殿下職分，止於監國撫軍、問安視膳而已，此外予奪賞罰之權，自在君父。

translations.literal: Moreover Your Highness's duty is only to oversee the state, comfort the armies, inquire after health, and attend meals—beyond this the power of granting, taking, rewarding, and punishing rests with ruler and father.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness's duty is to oversee the state, comfort the armies, and attend the emperor's health and meals—reward and punishment belong to the throne alone.

sentences.zh: 今方毓德春宮，而使諫臣結舌，凶人肆志，豈惟君父徒擁虛器，而天下蒼生，亦將奚望！」

translations.literal: Now just as virtue is nurtured in the Eastern Palace, yet remonstrating ministers are silenced and vicious men indulge their will—not only does ruler and father hold an empty vessel in vain, but the living people of the realm—what will they look to!'
translations.idiomatic: You are still cultivating virtue in the Eastern Palace, yet remonstrators are silenced and villains run free—not only does the emperor hold an empty title, but what hope is left for the people?'

sentences.zh: 疏上，皇太子怒，令御史大夫老的沙諭祖仁，以謂「台臣所言雖是，但橐驩等俱無是事，御史糾言不實，已與美除。

translations.literal: The memorial went up; the heir apparent was angry and ordered Censor-in-Chief Lao Desha to instruct Zuren, saying: 'What the censorate officials said is so, but Tuo Huan and the others had none of these matters; the censors' impeachment was untrue and they have already been given fine appointments.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was angry and had Censor-in-Chief Lao Desha tell Zuren: 'The censorate may be right in form, but Tuo Huan and the rest did nothing wrong; the charges were false and they have already been given good posts.

sentences.zh: 昔裕宗為皇太子，兼中書令、樞密使，凡軍國重事合奏聞者，乃許上聞，非獨我今日如是也。」

translations.literal: Formerly when Prince Yu was heir apparent he concurrently held Secretariat Director and Privy Council Commissioner; all important military and state matters that should be memorialized were only then permitted to be reported—not only today is it so.'
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yu was heir apparent he also held the chancellorship and privy council; only major military and state matters were reported upward. It is not only today that this is so.'

sentences.zh: 祖仁乃復上疏言：「御史所劾，得於田野之間，殿下所詢，不出宮牆之外，所以全此二人者，止緣不見其奸。

translations.literal: Zuren then again submitted a memorial saying: 'What the censors impeached was obtained among fields and villages; what Your Highness inquired did not go outside the palace walls—therefore to spare these two men is only because their wickedness is not seen.
translations.idiomatic: Zuren wrote again: 'The censors learned the truth in the countryside; Your Highness inquired only within the palace walls. You spare these two only because you do not see their crimes.

sentences.zh: 昔唐德宗云：'人言盧杞奸邪，朕殊不覺。

translations.literal: Formerly Tang Dezong said: 'People say Lu Qi is wicked and depraved—I am wholly unaware.'
translations.idiomatic: Tang Dezong once said, 'People say Lu Qi is wicked—I notice nothing.'

sentences.zh: '使德宗早覺，杞安得相？

translations.literal: Had Dezong early perceived it, how could Qi have become chief minister?
translations.idiomatic: Had Dezong seen it early, how could Qi have become chief minister?

sentences.zh: 是杞之奸邪，當時知之，獨德宗不知爾。

translations.literal: That Qi's wickedness and depravity was known at the time—only Dezong did not know it.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone at court knew Qi's wickedness—only Dezong did not.

sentences.zh: 今此二人，亦皆奸邪，舉朝知之，在野知之，天下知之，獨殿下未知耳。

translations.literal: Now these two men are also all wicked and depraved; the whole court knows it, those in the wilds know it, the realm knows it—only Your Highness does not know.
translations.idiomatic: These two are wicked too—the court knows, the countryside knows, the realm knows—only Your Highness does not.

sentences.zh: 且裕宗既領軍國重事，理宜先閱其綱。

translations.literal: Moreover, since Prince Yu already oversaw important military and state matters, he should first have reviewed their essentials.
translations.idiomatic: Since Prince Yu oversaw military and state affairs, he should first have read the essentials himself.

sentences.zh: 若至臺諫封章，自是御前開拆，假使必皆經由東宮，君父或有差失，諫臣有言，太子將使之聞奏乎，不使之聞奏乎？

translations.literal: As for censorate and remonstrance sealed memorials, they are by nature opened before the sovereign; suppose they must all pass through the Eastern Palace—if ruler and father have some fault and remonstrating ministers have words, will the heir apparent have them reported or not have them reported?
translations.idiomatic: Censorate memorials are opened before the emperor. If they must all pass through the Eastern Palace and the emperor errs, will the prince report the remonstrance or withhold it?

sentences.zh: 使之聞奏，則傷其父心，不使聞奏，則陷父於惡，殿下將安所處！

translations.literal: If you have them reported, you wound your father's heart; if you do not have them reported, you trap your father in evil—where will Your Highness stand!
translations.idiomatic: Report it and you wound your father; withhold it and you trap him in wrong—where then will Your Highness stand!

sentences.zh: 如知此說，則今日糾劾之章，不宜阻矣，御史不宜斥矣。

translations.literal: If you know this doctrine, then today's memorials of impeachment should not be blocked and censors should not be driven out.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing this, you should not block today's impeachment or drive out the censors.

sentences.zh: 斥其人而美其除，不知御史所言，為天下國家乎，為一身官爵乎？

translations.literal: Driving out the men while beautifying their appointments—do you not know whether what the censors said was for the realm and state or for a single body's office and rank?
translations.idiomatic: You drive out the accusers and reward the accused—do you think the censors spoke for the realm or for their own offices?

sentences.zh: 斥者去，來者言，言者無窮，而美除有限，殿下又安所處？」

translations.literal: Those driven out go; those who come speak; speakers are without end while fine appointments are limited—where again will Your Highness stand?'
translations.idiomatic: Drive one out and another speaks; speakers are endless but fine posts are few—where will Your Highness stand then?'

sentences.zh: 祖仁疏既再上，即辭職，而御史下至吏卒皆辭閒。

translations.literal: After Zuren's memorial was submitted again, he at once resigned, and censors down to clerks and soldiers all resigned their posts.
translations.idiomatic: After Zuren submitted again he resigned, and censors down to clerks all quit their posts.

sentences.zh: 於是皇太子以其事聞，樸不花、橐驩乃皆辭退。

translations.literal: Thereupon the heir apparent reported the matter upward, and Puhua and Tuo Huan then both resigned and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent reported upward, and Puhua and Tuo Huan both resigned.

sentences.zh: 而天子令老的沙諭旨祖仁等，祖仁复上書天子曰：「祖宗以天下傳之陛下，今乃壞亂不可救藥，雖曰天運使然，亦陛下刑賞不明之所致也。

translations.literal: But the Son of Heaven ordered Lao Desha to convey the imperial intent to Zuren and the others. Zuren again wrote to the Son of Heaven: 'The ancestors transmitted the realm to Your Majesty; now it is ruined and beyond saving by medicine—though one may say Heaven's mandate makes it so, it is also caused by Your Majesty's rewards and punishments not being clear.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Lao Desha convey his will to Zuren and the rest. Zuren wrote again to the emperor: 'The ancestors gave you the realm; now it is ruined beyond remedy. You may call it fate, but unclear rewards and punishments are also to blame.

sentences.zh: 且區區二豎，猶不能除，況於大者！

translations.literal: Moreover these petty two eunuchs you still cannot remove—how much more the great!
translations.idiomatic: You cannot remove two petty eunuchs—what of greater evils!

sentences.zh: 願陛下俯從臺諫之言，擯斥此二人，不令其以辭退為名，成其奸計，使海內皆知陛下信賞必罰自二人始，則將士孰不效力。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to bow to the words of the censorate and remonstrance offices, drive out these two men, and not let them use resignation as a name to accomplish their wicked scheme, so that within the seas all know Your Majesty's faithful rewards and sure punishments begin with these two—then which officer and soldier will not exert strength?
translations.idiomatic: Accept the censors' counsel, drive these two out, and do not let resignation be their trick. Let the realm see that faithful reward and sure punishment begin with them—then who among the troops will not fight?

sentences.zh: 天下可全，而有以還祖宗之舊，若猶優柔不斷，則臣寧有餓死於家，誓不與之同朝，牽聯及禍，以待後世正人同罪。」

translations.literal: The realm can be preserved and there can be means to return to the ancestors' former state; if you still are gentle and cannot decide, then your servant would rather starve at home, swearing not to serve in the same court, dragged into calamity, awaiting later generations' upright men to share the guilt.'
translations.idiomatic: The realm can be saved and the founders' order restored. If you still hesitate, I would rather starve at home than serve this court, and await later ages to judge us alike.'

sentences.zh: 書奏，天子大怒，而是時侍御史李國鳳亦上疏，言此二人必當斥，於是台臣自老的沙以下皆左遷，而祖仁出為甘肅行省參知政事。

translations.literal: The letter was submitted; the Son of Heaven was greatly angry. At this time Attending Censor Li Guofeng also submitted a memorial saying these two men must be driven out; thereupon censorate officials from Lao Desha downward were all demoted, and Zuren went out as associate administrator of the Gansu Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious. Attending Censor Li Guofeng also said the two must be expelled. Every censor from Lao Desha down was demoted, and Zuren was sent to Gansu as associate administrator.

sentences.zh: 時天極寒，衣

translations.literal: The weather was extremely cold; his clothes
translations.idiomatic: The weather was bitterly cold; his clothes

sentences.zh: 單甚，以弱女託於其友硃毅，即日就道。

translations.literal: were very thin; he entrusted his young daughter to his friend Zhu Yi and that same day took the road.
translations.idiomatic: were very thin; he left his young daughter with his friend Zhu Yi and set out the same day.

sentences.zh: 明年七月，孛羅帖木兒入中書為丞相，除祖仁山北道肅政廉訪使，召拜國子祭酒，遷樞密副使，累上疏言軍政利害，不報，辭職。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the next year Boluo Temur entered the Secretariat as chief councillor; Zuren was removed as surveillance commissioner of the Shanbei Circuit, summoned as Rector of the National University, transferred to vice commissioner of the Privy Council, repeatedly submitted memorials on the benefits and harms of military government without response, and resigned.
translations.idiomatic: The next year in the seventh month Boluo Temur became chief councillor. Zuren was made Shanbei surveillance commissioner, then rector of the National University, then vice commissioner of the Privy Council. He memorialized repeatedly on military affairs without answer and resigned.

sentences.zh: 除翰林學士，遂拜中書參知政事。
