translations.literal: He was removed as Hanlin academician and then appointed associate administrator of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He became Hanlin academician, then associate administrator of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 是時天下亂已甚，而祖仁性剛直，遇事與時宰論議數不合，乃超授其階榮祿大夫，而仍還翰林為學士，尋遷太常禮儀​​院使。

translations.literal: At this time disorder in the realm was already extreme, yet Zuren's nature was stern and upright; in affairs he often disagreed in debate with the chief ministers of the time, so they extraordinarily granted him the rank Grand Master of Glorious Blessing but still returned him to the Hanlin as academician, and soon transferred him to director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was already in extreme disorder; Zuren was stiff and upright and often clashed with the chief ministers. They promoted him to Grand Master of Glorious Blessing but sent him back to the Hanlin, then made him director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Ritual.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，大明兵已取山東，而朝廷方疑擴廓帖木兒有不臣之心，專立撫軍院，總兵馬以備之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year the Great Ming army had already taken Shandong, while the court was just suspecting Kozha Temur of disloyal intent and specially established the Pacification Army Commission to gather troops and horses to guard against him.
translations.idiomatic: In year 27 the Ming army had taken Shandong while the court suspected Kozha Temur of disloyalty and set up a Pacification Army Commission to guard against him.

sentences.zh: 祖仁乃與翰林學士承旨王時、待制黃哻、編修黃肅伏闕上書言：「近者南軍侵陷全齊，不踰月而逼畿甸，朝廷雖命丞相也速出師，軍馬數少，勢力孤危，而中原諸軍，左牽右掣，調度失宜，京城四面，茫無屏蔽，宗社安危，正在今日。

translations.literal: Zuren then with Hanlin Academician-in-Chief Wang Shi, Awaiting Edict Huang Xia, and Compiler Huang Su prostrated themselves at the gate and submitted a letter saying: 'Recently the southern army invaded and overran all Qi; in not more than a month they pressed the capital region. Though the court ordered Chief Councillor Yeshu to lead troops out, the army and horses were few in number and the force lonely and perilous, while the armies of the central plain were pulled left and checked right and deployment was unfitting; on all four sides of the capital city there was blankly no screen—the altars of state and their safety hang on this very day.
translations.idiomatic: Zuren with Wang Shi, Huang Xia, and Huang Su prostrated themselves at the palace gate and wrote: 'The southern army has overrun Qi and in less than a month threatens the capital. Yeshu was sent out with too few troops while central armies are pulled every way and deployment fails. The capital has no shield on any side—the fate of the dynasty hangs on today.

sentences.zh: 臣愚等以為馭天下之勢，當論其輕重強弱，遠近先後，不宜膠於一偏，狃於故轍。

translations.literal: Your foolish servants consider that in steering the momentum of the realm one should discuss its light and heavy, strong and weak, far and near, first and after—not stick to one partial view or cling to old ruts.
translations.idiomatic: We believe that steering the realm requires weighing what is light and heavy, strong and weak, near and far—not clinging to one fixed view or old habit.

sentences.zh: 前日南軍僻在一方，而擴廓帖木兒近在肘腋，勢將竊持國柄，故宜先於致討，則南軍遠而輕，而擴廓帖木兒近而重也。

translations.literal: Formerly the southern army was secluded in one region while Kozha Temur was close at the elbow and armpit and his momentum would steal and hold the handles of state—therefore one should first move to punish him; then the southern army was far and light while Kozha Temur was near and heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the southern army was distant while Kozha Temur was at your elbow and seemed ready to seize power—so attacking him first was right: the southern threat was far and lighter, Kozha Temur near and heavier.

sentences.zh: 今擴廓帖木兒勢已窮蹙，而南軍突至，勢將不利於宗社，故宜先於救難，則擴廓帖木兒弱而輕，南軍近而重也。

translations.literal: Now Kozha Temur's momentum is already cornered and exhausted while the southern army has suddenly arrived and its momentum will be unfavorable to the altars of state—therefore one should first rescue from calamity; then Kozha Temur is weak and light while the southern army is near and heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Now Kozha Temur is broken while the southern army has struck—disaster threatens the dynasty. Rescue comes first: Kozha Temur is now weak and light, the southern army near and heavy.

sentences.zh: 陛下寬仁涵育，皇太子賢明英斷，當此之時，宜審其輕重強弱，改弦更張，而撫軍諸官，亦宜以公天下為心，審時制宜。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is generous and nurturing; the heir apparent is worthy, bright, and decisive—at this time you should examine light and heavy, strong and weak, change the string and stretch anew, and the officials of the Pacification Army Commission should also take the public realm as heart and examine the time to fit measures.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is generous; the heir apparent is able and decisive. Now you should weigh priorities, change policy, and the Pacification Army officials should serve the public good and adapt to the hour.

sentences.zh: 今擴廓帖木兒黨與離散，豈能復振，若止分撥一軍逼襲，必就擒獲，其餘彼中見調一應軍馬，令其倍道東行，勤王赴難，與也速等聲勢相援，仍遣重臣，分道宣諭催督，庶幾得宜。

translations.literal: Now Kozha Temur's faction and followers are scattered—how can he revive? If you only allot one army to press and attack, he will surely be captured; the rest of the armies there presently deployed should be ordered to march double speed east, hasten to the throne and rush to the calamity, support Yeshu and others in momentum, and still send great ministers by separate routes to proclaim and urge—then perhaps it will be fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Kozha Temur's faction is scattered and cannot revive. Send one army to take him—it will succeed. Order the rest of his troops to march east at forced pace to relieve the capital and support Yeshu, with great ministers sent to urge them on—that may yet suffice.

sentences.zh: 如復膠於前說，動以言者為擴廓帖木兒遊說，而鉗天下之口，不幸猝有意外之變，朝廷亦不得聞，而天下之事去矣。」

translations.literal: If you again stick to the former doctrine, moving to treat speakers as Kozha Temur's lobbyists and clamp the mouths of the realm—if unhappily there is a sudden unexpected change, the court also will not hear of it, and the affairs of the realm are gone.'
translations.idiomatic: If you cling to the old view, call every speaker Kozha Temur's agent, and silence the realm—when sudden disaster comes the court will not hear of it, and the realm is lost.'

sentences.zh: 書上，不報。

translations.literal: The letter went up; no response.
translations.idiomatic: No answer came.

sentences.zh: 十二月，祖仁又上書皇太子，言：「近日降詔，削河南軍馬之權，雖所當然，然此項軍馬，終為南軍之所忌。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Zuren again wrote the heir apparent, saying: 'Recently an edict was issued reducing the authority of the Henan armies and horses—though fitting in itself, yet these armies and horses are in the end what the southern army fears.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Zuren wrote the heir apparent again: 'The recent edict stripping the Henan armies of authority is understandable, yet those troops are what the southern army most fears.

sentences.zh: 設使其有悖逆之心，朝廷以忠臣待之，其心愧沮，將何所施。

translations.literal: Suppose they have a rebellious heart—if the court treats them as loyal ministers, their hearts ashamed and dejected, what will they apply?
translations.idiomatic: If they were disloyal, treating them as loyal ministers would shame and discourage them—what could they then do?

sentences.zh: 今未有所見，遽以此名加之，彼若甘心以就此名，其害有不可言者。

translations.literal: Now nothing has yet been seen, yet we hastily add this title to him; if he willingly accepts this name, the harm is beyond words.
translations.idiomatic: We have seen nothing to justify it, yet this title is being imposed on him in haste; if he willingly accepts it, the harm will be beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 朝廷苟善用之，豈無所助。

translations.literal: If the court would only employ him well, would there not be some assistance?
translations.idiomatic: If the court would only make good use of him, would it not gain some real help?

sentences.zh: 然人皆知之而不敢言者，誠恐誣以受財遊說罪名，無所昭雪也。

translations.literal: Yet everyone knows this and dares not speak, truly fearing to be falsely charged with the crime of accepting bribes for lobbying, with no way to clear their name.
translations.idiomatic: Yet everyone knows this and dares not speak out, for fear of being falsely accused of taking bribes to lobby on his behalf, with no hope of vindication.

sentences.zh: 況聞擴廓帖木兒屢上書疏，明其心曲，是其心未絕於朝廷，以待朝廷之開悟。

translations.literal: Moreover it is heard that Kocho Temür has repeatedly submitted memorials clarifying his inner thoughts—that his heart has not severed ties with the court, awaiting the court's enlightenment.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Kocho Temür is said to have submitted memorial after memorial laying bare his intentions, showing that his loyalty to the court is not yet broken and that he waits for the court to come to its senses.

sentences.zh: 當今為朝廷計者，不過戰、守、遷三事。

translations.literal: For the court to plan today, there are no more than three matters: fight, hold, or relocate.
translations.idiomatic: For the court to plan at present, there are only three courses: to fight, to hold, or to relocate.

sentences.zh: 以言乎戰，則資其掎角之勢；

translations.literal: Speaking of fighting, one may draw on his flanking support;
translations.idiomatic: If one speaks of fighting, one may draw on his power to strike from two sides;

sentences.zh: 以言乎守，則望其勤王之師；

translations.literal: speaking of holding, one looks to his armies that come to rescue the throne;
translations.idiomatic: if one speaks of holding the capital, one looks to his armies marching to rescue the throne;

sentences.zh: 以言乎遷，則假其籓衛之力。

translations.literal: speaking of relocating, one borrows his power as a border guardian.
translations.idiomatic: if one speaks of relocating the court, one may borrow his strength as a frontier defender.

sentences.zh: 極力勉厲使行，猶恐遲晚，豈可使數万之師，棄置於一方。

translations.literal: We exert ourselves to the utmost to urge them to march, yet still fear it is too late—how can tens of thousands of troops be abandoned in one place?
translations.idiomatic: We strain every effort to urge them to march, yet still fear it may already be too late—how can tens of thousands of troops be left idle in one region?

sentences.zh: 當此危急之秋，宗社存亡，僅在旦夕，不幸一日有唐玄宗倉卒之出，則是以祖宗百年之宗社，朝廷委而棄之，此時雖欲碎首殺身，何濟於事！

translations.literal: At this critical juncture, the altars of state hang between survival and ruin from dawn to dusk; if unhappily one day there should be a hasty flight like Emperor Xuanzong of Tang, then the altars painstakingly built over a hundred years by our ancestors would be cast aside by the court—at that moment, even if one shattered one's head and gave one's life, what use would it be!
translations.idiomatic: At this hour of crisis, the fate of the altars of state hangs by a thread from one dawn to the next; if, heaven forbid, the court should one day flee in haste as Emperor Xuanzong of Tang once did, then the altars our forebears built over a century would be abandoned—and at that point, even smashing one's head and laying down one's life would avail nothing.

sentences.zh: 故今不復避忌，惟以宗社存亡為重，奉疏以聞。」

translations.literal: Therefore I no longer avoid taboo subjects; taking only the survival of the altars as paramount, I respectfully submit this memorial for Your Majesty's hearing.'
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I no longer hold back for fear of giving offense; I take only the survival of the altars of state as my concern and respectfully submit this memorial for Your Majesty's hearing.'

sentences.zh: 疏上，亦不報。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, there was again no response.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted, but again there was no reply.

sentences.zh: 二十八年秋，大明兵進壓近郊，有旨命祖仁及同僉太常禮儀院事王遜誌等載太廟神主，從皇太子北行。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the twenty-eighth year, as the Great Ming army pressed close to the suburbs, an edict ordered Zuren and Vice Commissioner of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Wang Xunzhi and others to carry the spirit tablets of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and follow the Crown Prince north.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the twenty-eighth year, as the Ming armies pressed toward the suburbs, an edict ordered Zuren and Wang Xunzhi, Vice Commissioner of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, together with others to carry the spirit tablets from the Imperial Ancestral Temple and follow the Crown Prince north.

sentences.zh: 祖仁等乃奏曰：「天子有大事出，則載主以行，從皇太子，非禮也。」

translations.literal: Zuren and the others then memorialized: "When the Son of Heaven departs on a great emergency, he carries the spirit tablets with him—but to follow the Crown Prince is not according to ritual."
translations.idiomatic: Zuren and his colleagues then memorialized: "When the Son of Heaven departs on a grave emergency, he carries the spirit tablets with him—but to follow the Crown Prince is not according to ritual."

sentences.zh: 帝然之，還守太廟以俟命。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved; they returned to guard the Imperial Ancestral Temple awaiting further orders.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed; they returned to guard the Imperial Ancestral Temple and await further orders.

sentences.zh: 俄而天子北奔，祖仁守神主，不果從。

translations.literal: Soon the Son of Heaven fled north; Zuren guarded the spirit tablets and did not go after all.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Son of Heaven fled north; Zuren remained to guard the spirit tablets and did not go in the end.

sentences.zh: 八月二日，京城破，將出健德門，為亂軍所害，時年五十五。

translations.literal: On the second day of the eighth month the capital fell; as he was about to exit the Jiande Gate, he was killed by mutinous troops. He was fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: On the second day of the eighth month the capital fell; as he was about to leave by the Jiande Gate, he was killed by mutinous troops. He was fifty-five years old.

sentences.zh: 祖仁一目眇，貌寢，身短瘠，而語音清亮，議論偉然，負氣剛正，似不可犯者。

translations.literal: Zuren had one blind eye, plain features, a short thin body, yet his voice was clear and bright, his arguments imposing; proud and upright in spirit, he seemed not one to be crossed.
translations.idiomatic: Zuren had one blind eye, plain features, and a short, spare frame, yet his voice rang clear and his discourse was imposing; proud and upright in spirit, he seemed a man not to be crossed.

sentences.zh: 其學博而精，自天文、地理、律曆、兵乘、術數、百家之說，皆通其要。

translations.literal: His learning was broad and refined; from astronomy, geography, calendrical science, military doctrine, divination, and the teachings of the hundred schools, he mastered their essentials.
translations.idiomatic: His learning was broad and deep; from astronomy, geography, calendrics, military science, divination, and the teachings of the hundred schools, he had mastered their essentials.

sentences.zh: 為文簡質，而詩清麗，世多稱傳之。

translations.literal: His prose was plain and unadorned, while his poetry was clear and lovely; the world widely praised and circulated his works.
translations.idiomatic: His prose was plain and spare, his poetry clear and graceful; the world widely praised and circulated his writings.

sentences.zh: 王遜志，字文敏，惲之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Wang Xunzhi, style name Wenmin, was the great-grandson of Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xunzhi, whose style name was Wenmin, was the great-grandson of Yun.

sentences.zh: 以廕授侍儀司通事舍人，歷隰州判官、大寧縣尹，擢陝西行台監察御史，累遷僉漢中、河西、山北三道肅政廉訪司事，入為工部員外郎，遷禮部郎中，拜監察御史。

translations.literal: By yin privilege he was appointed Attendant of the Ceremonial Office of the Palace Attendants; he served as judge of Xi Prefecture and magistrate of Daning County, was promoted to investigating censor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat, and rose through successive appointments as commissioner of the Surveillance Commissions of the Hanzhong, Hexi, and Shanbei circuits; he entered the capital as vice director of the Ministry of Works, was transferred to director of rites in the Ministry of Rites, and was appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Through hereditary privilege he entered service as an attendant in the Ceremonial Office, then served as judge of Xi Prefecture and magistrate of Daning County; he was promoted to investigating censor on the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat and rose through successive posts as commissioner on the Surveillance Commissions of the Hanzhong, Hexi, and Shanbei circuits; he entered the capital as vice director of the Ministry of Works, became director of rites in the Ministry of Rites, and was appointed investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 劾詹事不蘭奚、平章宜童皆逆臣子孫，當屏諸遐裔。

translations.literal: He impeached the Chamberlain for the Heir Apparent Bolanxi and the Grand Councillor Yitong, both descendants of traitorous ministers, stating they should be banished to distant borderlands.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached the Chamberlain for the Heir Apparent Bolanxi and the Grand Councillor Yitong, both descendants of traitorous ministers, arguing that they should be banished to distant borderlands.

sentences.zh: 除太府少監，出為江西廉訪副使，召僉太常禮儀院事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Junior Supervisor of the Imperial Storehouse, then sent out as Deputy Commissioner of the Jiangxi Surveillance Commission, and later recalled as Vice Commissioner of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Junior Supervisor of the Imperial Storehouse, then sent out as Deputy Commissioner of the Jiangxi Surveillance Commission, and later recalled to serve as Vice Commissioner of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 京城不守，公卿爭出降，遜志獨家居，衣冠而坐。

translations.literal: When the capital could no longer be held, the high officials scrambled to surrender; Xunzhi alone remained at home, seated in full court dress.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell, the high officials rushed to surrender; Xunzhi alone stayed at home, seated in full court dress.

sentences.zh: 其友中政院判官王翼來告曰：「新朝寬大，不惟不死，且仍與官，盍出詣官自言狀。」

translations.literal: His friend Wang Yi, judge of the Central Secretariat for Palace Affairs, came and told him: "The new dynasty is magnanimous—you will not only escape death but even retain office. Why not go present yourself and state your case?"
translations.idiomatic: His friend Wang Yi, a judge of the Central Secretariat for Palace Affairs, came and urged him: "The new dynasty is magnanimous—you will not only be spared death but may even keep your office. Why not go to the authorities and present yourself?"

sentences.zh: 遜志艴然斥之曰：「君既自不忠，又誘人為不義耶！」

translations.literal: Xunzhi flushed with anger and rebuked him: "You are disloyal yourself, and now you lure others into disloyalty as well!"
translations.idiomatic: Xunzhi flushed with anger and rebuked him: "You are disloyal yourself—must you now lure others into disloyalty as well?"

sentences.zh: 因戒其子曰；

translations.literal: He then admonished his son, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He then admonished his son, saying:

sentences.zh: 「汝謹繼吾宗。」

translations.literal: "You must carefully carry on our family line."
translations.idiomatic: "You must carefully carry on our family line."

sentences.zh: 即自投井中死。

translations.literal: With that he cast himself into a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: With that he cast himself into a well and died.

sentences.zh: ○成遵

translations.literal: ○ Cheng Zun
translations.idiomatic: ○ Cheng Zun

sentences.zh: 成遵，字誼叔，南陽穰縣人也。

translations.literal: Cheng Zun, style name Yishu, was a native of Xiang County in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Zun, whose style name was Yishu, was a native of Xiang County in Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 幼敏悟，讀書日記數千百言。

translations.literal: As a child he was quick and perceptive; in reading he could memorize several thousand characters a day.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was quick-witted; in his reading he could memorize several thousand characters in a single day.

sentences.zh: 年十五，喪父。

translations.literal: At fifteen he lost his father.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of fifteen he lost his father.

sentences.zh: 家貧，勤苦不廢學問。

translations.literal: His family was poor, yet through hard toil he never abandoned his studies.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor, yet through hard labor he never abandoned his studies.

sentences.zh: 二十能文章。

translations.literal: At twenty he could write accomplished essays.
translations.idiomatic: By twenty he could write accomplished essays.

sentences.zh: 時郡中先輩無治進士業者，遵欲為，以不合程式為患。

translations.literal: At that time none of the senior scholars in the prefecture pursued the jinshi curriculum; Zun wished to do so but worried that his work did not conform to the examination format.
translations.idiomatic: At that time none of the senior scholars in the prefecture had pursued the jinshi curriculum; Zun wished to do so but worried that his compositions did not fit the examination format.

sentences.zh: 一日，憤然曰：「《四書》、《五經》，吾師也。

translations.literal: One day he said in anger: "The Four Books and the Five Classics are my teachers.
translations.idiomatic: One day he said in exasperation: "The Four Books and the Five Classics are my teachers.

sentences.zh: 文無逾於《史》、《漢》、韓、柳。

translations.literal: In prose nothing surpasses the Records, the Han histories, Han Yu, and Liu Zongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In prose nothing surpasses the Records, the Han histories, Han Yu, and Liu Zongyuan.

sentences.zh: 區區科舉之作，何難哉。」

translations.literal: These petty examination compositions—what difficulty could there be?"
translations.idiomatic: These petty examination compositions—what could be so difficult about them?"

sentences.zh: 會楊惠初登第，來尹穰，遵乃書所作數十篇見之。

translations.literal: It happened that Yang Hui had just passed the examinations and came to serve as magistrate of Xiang; Zun then wrote out several dozen of his compositions and presented them to him.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Yang Hui, who had just passed the examinations, came to serve as magistrate of Xiang; Zun then copied out several dozen of his compositions and presented them to him.

sentences.zh: 惠撫卷大喜，語之曰：「以此取科第，如拾芥耳。」

translations.literal: Hui stroked the scrolls and was greatly pleased, saying to him: "With these to win the degree, it would be like picking up a mustard seed."
translations.idiomatic: Hui ran his hand over the scrolls and was delighted, telling him: "With writing like this to win the degree, it would be as easy as picking up a mustard seed from the ground."

sentences.zh: 至順辛未，至京師，受《春秋》業於夏鎮，遂入成均為國子生。

translations.literal: In the xinwei year of the Zhishun reign he went to the capital, studied the Spring and Autumn Annals under Xia Zhen, and entered the Imperial Academy as a National University student.
translations.idiomatic: In the xinwei year of the Zhishun reign he went to the capital, studied the Spring and Autumn Annals under Xia Zhen, and entered the Imperial Academy as a National University student.

sentences.zh: 時陳旅為助教，喜其文，數以語於奎章閣侍書學士虞集，集亟欲見之，旅令以己馬俾遵馳詣集。

translations.literal: At that time Chen Lü was an assistant instructor; he admired Zun's writing and repeatedly spoke of it to Yu Ji, Attendant Academician of the Kuizhang Pavilion; Ji was eager to meet him, and Lü lent his own horse so that Zun might ride posthaste to see Ji.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Chen Lü served as an assistant instructor; he admired Zun's writing and spoke of it again and again to Yu Ji, Attendant Academician of the Kuizhang Pavilion. Ji was eager to meet him, and Lü lent his own horse so that Zun could ride posthaste to see Ji.

sentences.zh: 集方有目疾，見遵來，迫而視之，曰；

translations.literal: Ji was then afflicted with an eye ailment; when he saw Zun arrive, he drew close to look at him and said:
translations.idiomatic: Ji was then suffering from an eye ailment; when he saw Zun arrive, he drew close to look at him and said:

sentences.zh: 「適觀生文，今見生貌，公輔器也。

translations.literal: "Having just read your essays, I now see your bearing—you are material for the highest offices.
translations.idiomatic: "Having just read your essays, I now see your bearing—you are destined for the highest offices.

sentences.zh: 吾老矣，恐不及見，生當自愛重也。」

translations.literal: I am old now and fear I shall not live to see it; you must cherish and value yourself."
translations.idiomatic: I am old now and fear I shall not live to see it; you must cherish yourself and hold yourself in esteem."

sentences.zh: 元統改元，中進士第，授將仕郎、翰林國史院編修官。

translations.literal: When the Yuantong reign began, he passed the jinshi examinations and was appointed Junior Gentleman and compiler in the Hanlin Academy National History Office.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuantong reign began, he passed the jinshi examinations and was appointed Junior Gentleman and compiler in the Hanlin Academy National History Office.

sentences.zh: 明年，預修泰定、明宗、文宗三朝實錄。

translations.literal: The following year he took part in compiling the Veritable Records of the Taiding, Mingzong, and Wenzong reigns.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he took part in compiling the Veritable Records of the Taiding, Mingzong, and Wenzong reigns.

sentences.zh: 後至元四年，升應奉翰林文字。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of the Later Zhiyuan reign he was promoted to Attendant Drafter in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Later Zhiyuan reign he was promoted to Attendant Drafter in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 五年，辟御史臺掾。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was recruited as a clerk of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was recruited as a clerk of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 至正改元，擢太常博士。

translations.literal: When the Zhizheng reign began, he was promoted to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhizheng reign began, he was promoted to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 明年，轉中書檢校，尋拜監察御史。

translations.literal: The following year he was transferred to Inspector of the Central Secretariat, and soon after was appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred to Inspector of the Central Secretariat, and soon after was appointed investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 扈從至上京，上封事，言天子宜慎起居，節嗜欲，以保養聖躬，聖躬安則宗社安矣。

translations.literal: Accompanying the court to Shangdu, he submitted a sealed memorial stating that the Son of Heaven should be careful in his daily conduct and restrain his appetites so as to preserve the sacred person; when the sacred person is secure, the altars of state are secure.
translations.idiomatic: Accompanying the court to Shangdu, he submitted a sealed memorial urging the Son of Heaven to be careful in his daily conduct and restrain his appetites so as to preserve his health; when the sovereign's person is secure, the altars of state are secure.

sentences.zh: 言甚迫切，帝改容稱善。

translations.literal: His words were very urgent; the Emperor changed expression and praised them.
translations.idiomatic: His words were urgent in the extreme; the Emperor's expression changed and he praised them.

sentences.zh: 又言臺察四事：一曰差遣臺臣，越職問事；

translations.literal: He also spoke of four matters concerning censorial oversight: first, dispatching censors beyond their duties to inquire into affairs;
translations.idiomatic: He also spoke of four matters concerning censorial oversight: first, dispatching censors beyond their duties to inquire into affairs;

sentences.zh: 二曰左遷御史，杜塞言路；

translations.literal: second, demoting investigating censors and blocking the path of remonstrance;
translations.idiomatic: second, demoting investigating censors and blocking the path of remonstrance;

sentences.zh: 三曰御史不思盡言，循敘求進；

translations.literal: third, censors who do not think to speak fully but seek advancement by seniority alone;
translations.idiomatic: third, censors who do not think to speak their minds fully but seek advancement by seniority alone;

sentences.zh: 四曰體覆廉訪聲跡不實，賢否混淆。

translations.literal: fourth, covering up false reports on the conduct and reputation of surveillance commissioners, so that the worthy and unworthy are confused.
translations.idiomatic: fourth, covering up false reports on the conduct and reputation of surveillance commissioners, so that the worthy and the unworthy are confused.

sentences.zh: 帝皆喜納之，諭台臣曰：「遵所言甚善，皆世祖風紀舊規也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased to accept them all and instructed the censors: "What Zun has said is excellent—all are the old regulations on conduct and discipline from the time of Emperor Shizu."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was pleased to accept them all and instructed the censors: "What Zun has said is excellent—all of it reflects the old regulations on conduct and discipline from the time of Emperor Shizu."

sentences.zh: 特賜上尊旌其忠。

translations.literal: He was specially granted fine wine in recognition of his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially granted fine wine in recognition of his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 遵又言江浙火災當賑恤，及劾火魯忽赤不法十事，皆從之。

translations.literal: Zun also said that the fire disaster in Jiang-Zhe should receive relief, and impeached Huoluhuochi on ten counts of misconduct—all were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Zun also urged that the fire disaster in Jiang-Zhe should receive relief, and impeached Huoluhuochi on ten counts of misconduct—all were adopted.

sentences.zh: 复上封事，言時務四事：一曰法祖宗，二曰節財用，三曰抑奔競，四曰明激勸。

translations.literal: He again submitted a sealed memorial on four matters of current policy: first, follow the ancestral models; second, economize expenditures; third, restrain frantic competition for office; fourth, clarify rewards and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: He again submitted a sealed memorial on four matters of current policy: first, follow the ancestral models; second, economize expenditures; third, restrain frantic competition for office; fourth, clarify rewards and encouragement.

sentences.zh: 奏入，帝稱善久之，命中書速議以行。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the Emperor praised it at length and ordered the Central Secretariat to deliberate quickly and put it into effect.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the Emperor praised it at length and ordered the Central Secretariat to deliberate quickly and put it into effect.

sentences.zh: 是歲，言事並舉劾凡七十餘事，皆指訐時弊，執政者惡之。

translations.literal: That year, in memorials and impeachments together he addressed more than seventy matters, all pointing at current abuses; those in power hated him.
translations.idiomatic: That year, in memorials and impeachments together he addressed more than seventy matters, all pointing at current abuses; those in power came to hate him.

sentences.zh: 三年，自刑部員外郎出為陝西行省員外郎，以母病辭歸。

translations.literal: In the third year he left his post as vice director of the Ministry of Punishments to become vice director of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat, but resigned and returned home on account of his mother's illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he left his post as vice director of the Ministry of Punishments to become vice director of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat, but resigned and returned home when his mother fell ill.

sentences.zh: 五年，丁母憂。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he entered mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 八年，擢僉淮東肅政廉訪司事，改禮部郎中，奉使山東、淮北察守令賢否，得循良者九人，貪懦者二十一人，奏之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was promoted to Commissioner of the Huaidong Surveillance Commission for Upholding Justice, then transferred to Director of Rites in the Ministry of Rites; commissioned to inspect the worthiness of prefectural and county officials in Shandong and north of the Huai, he found nine who were upright and diligent and twenty-one who were greedy or timid, and memorialized accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was promoted to Commissioner of the Huaidong Surveillance Commission, then transferred to Director of Rites in the Ministry of Rites; commissioned to inspect the worthiness of prefectural and county officials in Shandong and north of the Huai, he found nine who were upright and diligent and twenty-one who were greedy or timid, and memorialized accordingly.

sentences.zh: 九人者，賜上尊幣帛，仍加顯擢；

translations.literal: The nine were granted fine wine and silks and further given conspicuous promotion;
translations.idiomatic: The nine were granted fine wine and silks and further given conspicuous promotion;

sentences.zh: 其二十一人悉黜之。

translations.literal: the twenty-one were all dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: the twenty-one were all dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 九年，改刑部郎中，尋遷御史臺都事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was transferred to Director of Punishments in the Ministry of Punishments, and soon after was promoted to Chief Clerk of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was transferred to Director of Punishments in the Ministry of Punishments, and soon after was promoted to Chief Clerk of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 時台臣有嫉贓吏多以父母之憂免者，建論今後官吏，凡被案劾贓私，雖父母死，不許歸葬，須竟其獄，庶惡人不獲倖免。

translations.literal: At that time some censors, resenting that corrupt officials often escaped through mourning for their parents, proposed that henceforth whenever an official was impeached for graft, even if his parents died he should not be permitted to return home for burial but must await the conclusion of his case, so that evildoers might not escape.
translations.idiomatic: At that time some censors, resenting that corrupt officials often escaped prosecution by claiming mourning for their parents, proposed that henceforth whenever an official was impeached for graft, even if his parents died he should not be permitted to return home for burial but must await the conclusion of his case, so that evildoers might not escape.

sentences.zh: 遵曰：「惡人固可怒，然與人倫孰重？

translations.literal: Zun said: "Evildoers may indeed be enraging, but which weighs heavier—punishing them or human relations?
translations.idiomatic: Zun said: "Evildoers may indeed be enraging, but which weighs heavier—punishing them or the bonds of human relations?

sentences.zh: 且國家以孝治天下，寧失罪人千百，不可使天下有無親之吏。」

translations.literal: Moreover the state governs the realm through filial piety; better to let a thousand guilty men go than to have officials throughout the realm without parents."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the state governs the realm through filial piety; better to let a thousand guilty men go than to have officials throughout the realm who are without parents."

sentences.zh: 御史大夫是其言。

translations.literal: The Censor-in-Chief agreed with his words.
translations.idiomatic: The Censor-in-Chief agreed with his words.

sentences.zh: 升戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 十年，遷中書右司郎中。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to Director of the Right Department of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was transferred to Director of the Right Department of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時刑部獄按久而不決者積數百，遵與其僚分閱之，共議其輕重，各當其罪，未幾，無遺事。

translations.literal: At that time several hundred cases in the prisons of the Ministry of Punishments had long gone undecided; Zun and his colleagues divided them for review, deliberated together on their severity, and assigned to each its proper penalty; before long nothing remained unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: At that time several hundred cases in the prisons of the Ministry of Punishments had long gone undecided; Zun and his colleagues divided them for review, deliberated together on their severity, and assigned to each its proper penalty; before long nothing remained unresolved.

sentences.zh: 時有令輸粟補官，有匿其奸罪而入粟得七品雜流者，為怨家所告，有司議輸粟例，無有過不與之文，遵曰：「賣官鬻爵，已非盛典，況又賣官與姦淫之人，其將何以為治。

translations.literal: At that time there was an order allowing grain contributions in exchange for office; one man who concealed his crimes of debauchery and bought a seventh-rank miscellaneous post through grain was denounced by an enemy; the authorities debated the grain-contribution precedent, which had no provision denying office to those with prior offenses; Zun said: "Selling offices and titles is already no proper institution—how much less selling them to men guilty of debauchery; how then is government to be conducted?
translations.idiomatic: At that time there was an order allowing grain contributions in exchange for office; one man who concealed his crimes of debauchery and bought a seventh-rank miscellaneous post through grain was denounced by an enemy; the authorities debated the grain-contribution precedent, which had no provision denying office to those with prior offenses; Zun said: "Selling offices and titles is already no proper institution—how much less selling them to men guilty of debauchery; how then is government to be conducted?

sentences.zh: 必奪其敕，還其粟，著為令，乃可。」

translations.literal: His patent must be revoked, his grain returned, and this written into regulation—only then will it do."
translations.idiomatic: His patent must be revoked, his grain returned, and this written into regulation—only then will it suffice."

sentences.zh: 省臣從之。

translations.literal: The provincial officials agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial officials agreed.

sentences.zh: 除工部尚書。

translations.literal: He was appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 先是，河決白茅，鄆城、濟寧皆為巨浸。

translations.literal: Earlier the Yellow River had burst its banks at Baimao, and Yuncheng and Jining were both submerged in vast floods.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Yellow River had burst its banks at Baimao, and Yuncheng and Jining were both submerged in vast floods.

sentences.zh: 或言當築堤以遏水勢，或言必疏南河故道以殺水勢，而漕運使賈魯言：「必疏南河，塞北河，使復故道。

translations.literal: Some said dikes should be built to check the force of the waters, others that the old course of the southern river must be dredged to reduce it; but Jia Lu, Commissioner of Grain Transport, said: "The southern river must be dredged and the northern river blocked so that the old course may be restored.
translations.idiomatic: Some said dikes should be built to check the force of the waters, others that the old course of the southern river must be dredged to reduce it; but Jia Lu, Commissioner of Grain Transport, said: "The southern river must be dredged and the northern river blocked so that the old course may be restored.

sentences.zh: 役不大興，害不能已。」

translations.literal: Unless labor on a great scale is undertaken, the harm cannot be ended."
translations.idiomatic: Unless labor on a great scale is undertaken, the harm cannot be ended."

sentences.zh: 廷議莫能決。

translations.literal: Court deliberation could reach no decision.
translations.idiomatic: Court deliberation could reach no decision.

sentences.zh: 乃命遵偕大司農禿魯行視河，議其疏塞之方以聞。

translations.literal: The court then ordered Zun together with Tuolu, Grand Minister of Agriculture, to travel and inspect the river, deliberate on methods of dredging and blocking, and report.
translations.idiomatic: The court then ordered Zun together with Tuolu, Grand Minister of Agriculture, to travel and inspect the river, deliberate on methods of dredging and blocking, and report back.

sentences.zh: 十一年春，自濟寧、曹、濮、汴梁、大名，行數千里，掘井以量地形之高下，測岸以究水勢之淺深，遍閱史籍，博採輿論，以謂河之故道，不可得復，其議有八。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eleventh year, from Jining, Cao, Pu, Bianliang, and Daming, they traveled several thousand li, sinking wells to measure the heights and lows of the terrain and surveying the banks to investigate the shallows and depths of the waters; they read widely in historical records and gathered public opinion broadly, concluding that the river's old course could not be restored, and set forth eight points in their proposal.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eleventh year, from Jining, Cao, Pu, Bianliang, and Daming, they traveled several thousand li, sinking wells to measure the heights and lows of the terrain and surveying the banks to investigate the shallows and depths of the waters; they read widely in historical records and gathered public opinion broadly, concluding that the river's old course could not be restored, and set forth eight points in their proposal.

sentences.zh: 而丞相脫脫已先入賈魯之言，及遵與禿魯至，力陳不可，且曰：「濟寧、曹、鄆，連歲饑饉，民不聊生，若聚二十萬人於此地，恐後日之憂又有重於河患者。」

translations.literal: But the Chancellor Toghto had already been won over by Jia Lu's words; when Zun and Tuolu arrived, they strongly argued against it, saying: "Jining, Cao, and Yun have suffered famine year after year; the people can scarcely live. If two hundred thousand men are gathered in this place, I fear that troubles hereafter may outweigh the harm of the river itself."
translations.idiomatic: But the Chancellor Toghto had already been won over by Jia Lu's words; when Zun and Tuolu arrived, they argued forcefully against the plan, saying: "Jining, Cao, and Yun have suffered famine year after year; the people can scarcely survive. If two hundred thousand men are gathered in this place, I fear that troubles hereafter may outweigh the harm of the river itself."

sentences.zh: 脫脫怒曰：「汝謂民將反耶！」

translations.literal: Toghto said in anger: "Do you mean the people will rebel!"
translations.idiomatic: Toghto said in anger: "Do you mean the people will rebel!"

sentences.zh: 自辰至酉，辨論終不能入。

translations.literal: From the hour of chen to the hour of you they argued, but in the end could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: From morning until evening they argued, but in the end could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 明日，執政者謂遵曰：「修河之役，丞相意已定，且有人任其責矣，公其毋多言，幸為兩可之議。」

translations.literal: The next day those in power said to Zun: "On the river works the Chancellor's mind is already made up, and someone will bear responsibility for them; sir, speak no more on the matter—please offer a compromise proposal."
translations.idiomatic: The next day those in power said to Zun: "On the river works the Chancellor's mind is already made up, and someone will bear responsibility for them; sir, speak no more on the matter—please offer a compromise proposal."

sentences.zh: 遵曰：「腕可斷，議不可易也。」

translations.literal: Zun said: "My wrist may be cut off, but my position cannot be changed."
translations.idiomatic: Zun said: "My wrist may be cut off, but my position cannot be changed."

sentences.zh: 由是遂出為大都河間等處都轉運鹽使。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was sent out as Commissioner of Salt Transport for Dadu, Hejian, and other circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he was sent out as Commissioner of Salt Transport for Dadu, Hejian, and other circuits.

sentences.zh: 初，汝、汴二郡多富商，運司賴之，是時，汝寧盜起，侵汴境，朝廷調兵往討，括船運糧，以故舟楫不通，商販遂絕。

translations.literal: At first the Ru and Bian prefectures had many wealthy merchants on whom the transport office relied; at this time bandits rose in Runing and invaded the Bian border; the court dispatched troops to suppress them and requisitioned boats to transport grain, so that shipping was blocked and commerce ceased.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Ru and Bian prefectures had many wealthy merchants on whom the transport office relied; at this time bandits rose in Runing and invaded the Bian border; the court dispatched troops to suppress them and requisitioned boats to transport grain, so that shipping was blocked and commerce ceased.

sentences.zh: 遵隨事處宜，國課皆集。

translations.literal: Zun handled each matter as circumstances required, and all state revenues were collected.
translations.idiomatic: Zun handled each matter as circumstances required, and all state revenues were collected.

sentences.zh: 十四年，調武昌路總管。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was transferred to be Administrator of the Wuchang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was transferred to serve as Administrator of the Wuchang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 武昌自十二年為沔寇所殘毀，民死於兵疫者十六七，而大江上下，皆劇盜阻絕，米直翔踴，民心遑遑。

translations.literal: Wuchang had since the twelfth year been ravaged by bandits from the Han region; six or seven tenths of the people died in war and pestilence, while up and down the great river fierce robbers blocked all passage; the price of rice soared, and the people's hearts were in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchang had since the twelfth year been ravaged by bandits from the Han region; six or seven tenths of the people died in war and pestilence, while up and down the great river fierce robbers blocked all passage; the price of rice soared, and the people's hearts were in turmoil.

sentences.zh: 遵言於省臣，假軍儲鈔萬錠，募勇敢之士，具戈船，截兵境，且戰且行，糴粟於太平、中興，民賴以全活者眾。

translations.literal: Zun spoke to the provincial officials, borrowing ten thousand ingots of military grain notes, recruiting brave men, equipping armed boats, cutting across the war zone while fighting as they went, and buying grain at Taiping and Zhongxing; many people relied on this to survive.
translations.idiomatic: Zun spoke to the provincial officials, borrowing ten thousand ingots of military grain notes, recruiting brave men, equipping armed boats, cutting across the war zone while fighting as they went, and buying grain at Taiping and Zhongxing; many people relied on this to survive.

sentences.zh: 會省臣出師，遵攝省事，於是省中府中，惟遵一人。

translations.literal: When the provincial officials took the field, Zun acted in their stead in provincial affairs; thus in the provincial office and the prefectural office there was only Zun alone.
translations.idiomatic: When the provincial officials took the field, Zun acted in their stead in provincial affairs; thus in the provincial office and the prefectural office there was only Zun alone.

sentences.zh: 乃遠斥候，塞城門，籍民為兵，得五千餘人，設萬夫長四，配守四門，所以為防禦之備甚至，號令嚴肅，賞罰明當。

translations.literal: Thereupon he posted scouts far out, blocked the city gates, enrolled the people as soldiers, obtaining more than five thousand men, appointed four commanders of ten thousand, and assigned them to guard the four gates—the preparations for defense were carried to an extreme; orders were stern and rewards and punishments clear and fair.
translations.idiomatic: He posted scouts far out, sealed the gates, and enrolled more than five thousand men as militia, appointing four commanders of ten thousand to hold the four gates. Defensive preparations reached their utmost; his commands were austere and rewards and punishments exact.

sentences.zh: 賊船往來江中，終不敢近岸，城賴以安。

translations.literal: Rebel boats came and went on the river but in the end did not dare approach the shore; the city relied on this and was secure.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel vessels prowled the river but never dared come ashore; the city held secure.

sentences.zh: 十五年，擢江南行台治書侍御史，召拜參議中書省事。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was promoted to Investigating Censor of the Jiangnan Branch Secretariat and summoned to be appointed Associate Discussant of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15 he was promoted to investigating censor on the Jiangnan Branch Secretariat and summoned as an associate discussant in the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時河南之賊，數渡河而北，焚掠郡縣，上下視若常事。

translations.literal: At this time the bandits of Henan repeatedly crossed the river northward, burning and plundering prefectures and counties, while superiors and subordinates treated it as an ordinary matter.
translations.idiomatic: Henan bandits were crossing the Yellow River northward again and again, burning towns—and the court treated it as routine.

sentences.zh: 遵率左右司僚佐，持其牘詣丞相言曰：「今天下州縣，喪亂過半，河北之民稍安者，以天塹黃河為之障，賊兵雖至，不能飛渡，所以剝膚椎髓以供軍儲而無深怨者，視河南之民，猶得保其室家故也。

translations.literal: Zun led the officials of the Left and Right Secretariats, took their memorials and went to the Chancellor, saying: "Today, of all the prefectures and counties under Heaven, more than half lie in chaos and ruin. The reason the people north of the He are somewhat at peace is that the natural moat of the Yellow River serves as a barrier: though rebels may come, they cannot fly across it. The reason they flay their skin and pound their marrow to supply military stores yet bear no deep resentment is that, compared with the people of Henan, they can still keep their households intact.
translations.idiomatic: Zun led the left and right secretariat staff, memorial in hand, to the chancellor. He said: "More than half the empire's prefectures and counties lie in ruin. North of the Yellow River, folk endure only because the river is Heaven's moat—rebels cannot cross it at will. They strip themselves to fill the army's granaries yet resent little, for unlike Henan they still have roofs over their heads.

sentences.zh: 今賊北渡河而官軍不禦，是大河之險已不能守，河北之民復何所恃乎？

translations.literal: Now the bandits cross north while the government troops do not defend—this means the peril of the Great River can no longer be held, and upon what can the people north of the He rely?
translations.idiomatic: Now rebels cross north and our troops do not meet them—the river's defense is lost. What will Hebei trust hereafter?

sentences.zh: 河北民心一搖，國勢將如之何！」

translations.literal: If the hearts of the people north of the He are shaken once, what is to become of the national situation!"
translations.idiomatic: If Hebei's hearts waver once, what becomes of the realm?"

sentences.zh: 語未畢，哽咽不能言，宰相已下皆為之揮涕，乃以入奏。

translations.literal: Before he finished speaking he choked and could not continue; from the Chancellor down all wept for him, and then they entered to report to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He could not finish; voice breaking, he fell silent. From the chancellor down, all wept, and the matter went before the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝詔即遣使罪守河將帥，而守禦自是亦頗嚴。

translations.literal: The Emperor at once issued an edict sending envoys to punish the river-guarding generals, and from that time the river defenses also became rather strict.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor immediately sent envoys to discipline the river garrisons, and the northern defenses grew noticeably stricter.

sentences.zh: 先是，湖廣倪賊，質威順王之子，而遣人請降，求為湖廣行省平章，朝臣欲許者半，遵曰：「平章之職，亞宰相也。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Ni bandits of Huguang held the son of the Prince of Weishun as hostage and sent men to request surrender, asking to be appointed Grand Councillor of the Huguang Branch Secretariat; half the court ministers wished to grant it. Zun said: "The post of Grand Councillor ranks below the Chancellor alone.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Ni bandits of Huguang held the Prince of Weishun's son hostage and sued for surrender, demanding the Huguang grand councillorship. Half the court would grant it. Zun said: "Grand councillor ranks just below chancellor.

sentences.zh: 承平之時，雖德望漢人，抑而不與，今叛逆之賊，挾勢要求，輕以與之，如綱紀何！」

translations.literal: In times of peace, even eminent Han Chinese were held back and not granted it; now a rebellious bandit demands it by force—lightly to grant it, what of discipline and law!"
translations.idiomatic: In peace even worthy Han were refused this rank; shall we lightly hand it to rebels who extort it by force? What of law and order?"

sentences.zh: 或曰：「王子，世皇嫡孫也，不許，是棄之與賊，非親親之道也。」

translations.literal: Someone said: "The prince is the legitimate grandson of Shizu; if we refuse, we abandon him to the bandits—this is not the way of cherishing kin."
translations.idiomatic: Another said: "The prince is Emperor Shizu's own grandson; to refuse is to abandon him to bandits—not the way of kinship."

sentences.zh: 遵曰：「項羽執太公，欲烹之以挾高祖，高祖乃以分羹答之，奈何今以王子之故，廢天下大計乎！」

translations.literal: Zun said: "Xiang Yu seized the Grand Duke and wished to boil him to coerce Gaozu; Gaozu answered by offering to share the broth—how now can we set aside the great plan for all under Heaven because of a prince!"
translations.idiomatic: Zun said: "Xiang Yu seized Liu Bang's father and threatened to boil him; Gaozu replied that he wanted a bowl of the soup too. How shall we discard the empire's great design for one prince's sake?"

sentences.zh: 眾皆韙其論。

translations.literal: All approved his argument.
translations.idiomatic: All endorsed his view.

sentences.zh: 除治書侍御史，俄復入中書為參知政事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Investigating Censor, and soon reentered the Central Secretariat as Associate Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: He was made investigating censor, then soon reentered the Secretariat as associate councillor.

sentences.zh: 離省僅六日，丞相每決大議，則曰「姑少緩之」，眾莫曉其意，及遵拜執政，喜曰：「大政事今可決矣。」

translations.literal: Having left the Secretariat only six days, whenever the Chancellor decided a great matter he would say "Let us delay a little"; no one understood his meaning until Zun received the post of councillor, when he rejoiced and said: "Great affairs of state can now be decided."
translations.idiomatic: Zun had been out of the Secretariat only six days. On every weighty decision the chancellor said, "Let us wait"—none knew why—until Zun took office again, when he said joyfully, "Great matters can be settled now."

sentences.zh: 十七年，升中書左丞，階資善大夫，分省彰德。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was promoted to Left Vice Chancellor of the Central Secretariat, rank Senior Counselor for Goodness, and assigned to branch secretariat duty at Zhangde.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17 he rose to left vice chancellor, rank of Senior Counselor for Goodness, with detached duty at Zhangde.

sentences.zh: 是時，太平在相位，以事忤皇太子，皇太子深銜之，欲去之而未有以發，以為遵及參知政事趙中，皆太平黨也，遵、中兩人去，則太平之黨孤。

translations.literal: At this time Taiping held the chancellorship but had given offense to the heir apparent on some matter; the heir held a deep grudge and wished to remove him but had no occasion. He regarded Zun and Associate Councillor Zhao Zhong as both of Taiping's faction; if Zun and Zhao were removed, Taiping's party would stand alone.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping then held the chancellorship and had offended the heir apparent, who nursed deep resentment and sought his removal without pretext. He counted Zun and Zhao Zhong among Taiping's allies; remove them, he reasoned, and Taiping would stand alone.

sentences.zh: 十九年，用事者承望風旨，嗾寶坻縣尹鄧守禮弟鄧子初等，誣遵與參政趙中、參議蕭庸等六人皆受贓，皇太子命御史臺、大宗正府等官雜問之，鍛煉使成獄，遵等竟皆杖死，中外冤之。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year those in power, reading the wind of intent, incited Deng Zichu, younger brother of Baodi Magistrate Deng Shouli, and others to falsely accuse Zun, Councillor Zhao Zhong, Discussant Xiao Yong, and six men in all of taking bribes. The heir apparent ordered the Censorate, the Office of the Imperial Clan, and other officials jointly to interrogate them, forging the case until it stood complete; Zun and the rest were in the end all beaten to death, and within and without the court considered it an injustice.
translations.idiomatic: In year 19 men in power read the prince's mood and set Deng Zichu, brother of Baodi magistrate Deng Shouli, to frame Zun, Zhao Zhong, Xiao Yong, and six others for bribery. The heir had the Censorate and Imperial Clan Office examine them; the case was forged to completion, and all were flogged to death—a wrong mourned throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，御史臺臣辯明遵等皆誣枉，詔复給還其所授宣敕。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year censorate officials proved that Zun and the others had all been falsely wronged; an edict ordered restoration of the patents of appointment they had received.
translations.idiomatic: In year 24 the Censorate cleared them of false charges; an edict restored their commissions.

sentences.zh: ○曹鑑

translations.literal: ○ Cao Jian
translations.idiomatic: ○ Cao Jian

sentences.zh: 曹鑑，字克明，宛平人。

translations.literal: Cao Jian, style name Keming, was a man of Wanping.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Jian, style Keming, was from Wanping.

sentences.zh: 穎悟過人，舉止異常兒，既冠，南游，具通《五經》大義。

translations.literal: Quick-witted beyond others, in bearing unlike ordinary children, when he came of age he traveled south and thoroughly mastered the great meaning of the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: Precocious beyond his peers, unlike ordinary boys in manner, he traveled south after coming of age and mastered the substance of the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 大德五年，用翰林侍講學士郝彬薦，為鎮江淮海書院山長。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Dade, on the recommendation of Hanlin Lecturer Hao Bin, he became head mountain-chief of the Zhenjiang Huai-Hai Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In Dade 5, on Hanlin lecturer Hao Bin's recommendation, he became head of the Zhenjiang Huai-Hai Academy.

sentences.zh: 十一年，南行台中丞廉恆辟為掾史。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Branch Secretariat Commissioner Lian Heng recruited him as clerk.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 Commissioner Lian Heng of the southern Branch Secretariat took him on as clerk.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱，復起，補掾史，除興文署。

translations.literal: On mourning for his mother he returned to service, was restored as clerk, and was appointed to the Office for Promoting Literature.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning for his mother he returned, resumed as clerk, and was appointed to the Office for Promoting Literature.

sentences.zh: 命伴送安南使者，沿途問難倡和，應答如響，使者嘆服，以為中國有人。

translations.literal: Ordered to escort the Annamese envoy, along the road they posed hard questions and matched verses in reply; he answered like an echo, and the envoy sighed in admiration, taking it that the Middle Kingdom had men of talent.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to escort an Annamese envoy, he met every challenge and verse along the road with instant wit. The envoy marveled, saying China indeed had its men.

sentences.zh: 至治二年，授江浙行省左右司員外郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhizhi he was appointed Outside Vice-Director of the Left and Right Secretariats of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizhi 2 he was made outside vice-director on the Jiang-Zhe secretariat's left and right staffs.

sentences.zh: 明年，奉旨括釋氏白雲宗田，稽檢有方，不數月而事集，纖毫無擾。

translations.literal: The next year, by imperial order he surveyed the fields of the Buddhist Baiyun sect; his examination was well regulated, and within a few months the work was completed without the slightest disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he surveyed Baiyun Buddhist lands by imperial order—his audit so disciplined that within months the task was done without a whisper of trouble.

sentences.zh: 泰定七年，遷湖廣行省左右司員外郎。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taiding he was transferred to Outside Vice-Director on the Huguang Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiding 7 he was transferred to the same post on the Huguang secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時丞相忽剌歹怙勢恣縱，妄為威福，僚屬多畏避，鑑遇事徇理輒行，獨不為回撓。

translations.literal: At this time Chancellor Huladai relied on power and ran wild, willfully wielding authority and favor; colleagues mostly feared and shrank back, but Jian whenever reason lay with a matter carried it through alone, never bending.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Huladai then lorded his power, dispensing favors at will. Most staff shrank away; Jian alone pressed what reason required without bending.

sentences.zh: 湖北廉訪司舉鑑宜居風紀，不報。

translations.literal: The Huguang surveillance commission recommended Jian as fit to uphold discipline; no response came.
translations.idiomatic: The Huguang surveillance office recommended him for discipline posts; the court did not act.

sentences.zh: 天曆元年，調江浙財賦府副總管。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianli he was transferred to be Vice Administrator of the Jiang-Zhe Revenue Office.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianli 1 he was made vice administrator of Jiang-Zhe revenues.

sentences.zh: 屬淮、浙大水，民以災告，鑑損其賦什六七，勢家因而詭免者，鑑核實，諭令首輸。

translations.literal: When the Huai and Zhe regions suffered great floods and the people reported disaster, Jian reduced their tax by six or seven tenths; where powerful families sought fraudulent exemption he verified the facts and instructed them to pay first.
translations.idiomatic: Floods ravaged the Huai and Zhe; people pleaded disaster. He cut taxes six- or seven-tenths. Powerful houses claiming exemption he audited and ordered to pay up first.

sentences.zh: 元統二年，升同僉太常禮儀院，鑑習典故，達今古，凡禮樂、度數、名物，罔不周知。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuantong he was promoted to Vice Administrator of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; Jian was versed in precedents and comprehended past and present—ritual, music, measures, and naming of objects, none was not fully known to him.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuantong 2 he rose in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. Jian knew precedent through ages past and present—ritual, music, measures, and ritual objects left nothing unknown.

sentences.zh: 因集議明宗皇后祔廟事，援禮據經，辯析詳明，君子多之。

translations.literal: When the assembly discussed enshrining Empress Mingzong in the ancestral temple, he cited ritual and grounded it in the classics, analyzing in full detail; gentlemen widely praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Debating the enshrinement of Empress Mingzong, he argued from ritual and classics with luminous detail; men of discernment approved.

sentences.zh: 至元元年，以中大夫升禮部尚書，俄感疾而卒，年六十五。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhiyuan, with the rank of Grand Master of the Palace he was promoted to Minister of Rites, but soon took ill and died, aged sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 1 he rose to Minister of Rites as Grand Master of the Palace; illness soon took him at sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 追封譙郡侯，諡文穆。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Qiao and given the posthumous title Wenmu (Cultured and Solemn).
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Qiao with the posthumous name Wenmu.

sentences.zh: 鑑天性純孝，親族貧乏者，周恤恐後。

translations.literal: Jian's nature was pure filial piety; toward impoverished kin he aided and comforted, fearing to come last.
translations.idiomatic: Pure filial piety was his nature; to poor kin he gave aid, never behindhand.

sentences.zh: 歷官三十餘年，僦屋以居。

translations.literal: Over more than thirty years in office he rented a house to dwell in.
translations.idiomatic: For thirty years in office he lived in a rented house.

sentences.zh: 歿之日，家無餘貲，唯蓄書數千卷，皆鑑手較定。

translations.literal: On the day of his death his household had no surplus wealth, only several thousand volumes stored away, all collated by Jian's own hand.
translations.idiomatic: He died leaving no spare wealth, only several thousand books he had collated himself.

sentences.zh: 鑑為詩賦，尚《騷》、《雅》，作文法西漢，每篇成，學者爭相傳誦。

translations.literal: Jian wrote poetry and fu, esteeming the Chuci and Ya songs, composing prose after the model of the Western Han; whenever a piece was finished scholars vied to circulate and recite it.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry and fu looked to the Songs of Chu and the Book of Odes; his prose modeled the Western Han. Scholars passed each new piece from hand to hand.

sentences.zh: 有文集若干卷，藏於家。

translations.literal: He had a collection of writings in several scrolls, kept at home.
translations.idiomatic: A collection of writings in several juan remained in the family.

sentences.zh: 鑑任湖廣員外時，有故掾顧淵伯，以辰砂一包饋鑑，鑑漫爾置篋笥中。

translations.literal: When Jian served as outside vice-director in Huguang, a former clerk Gu Yuanbo presented a packet of cinnabar as a gift; Jian casually set it in a chest.
translations.idiomatic: As Huguang vice-director, former clerk Gu Yuanbo gave him a packet of cinnabar; Jian tossed it in a chest.

sentences.zh: 半載後，因欲合藥劑，命取視之，乃有黃金三兩雜其中，鑑驚歎曰：「淵伯以我為何如人也！」

translations.literal: Half a year later, wishing to compound medicine, he ordered it brought out and looked—it contained three taels of gold mixed in. Jian said in startled lament: "What sort of man did Yuanbo take me for!"
translations.idiomatic: Half a year later, preparing medicine, he had it brought out and found three taels of gold mixed in. He cried in dismay: "What sort of man did Yuanbo take me for!"

sentences.zh: 淵伯已歿，鑑呼其子歸之。

translations.literal: Yuanbo had already died; Jian called his son and returned it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanbo was dead; Jian summoned his son and returned the gold.

sentences.zh: 其廉慎不欺如此。

translations.literal: Such was his integrity, caution, and refusal to deceive.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his integrity that he would neither deceive nor be deceived.

sentences.zh: ○張翥

translations.literal: ○ Zhang Zhu
translations.idiomatic: ○ Zhang Zhu

sentences.zh: 張翥，字仲舉，晉寧人。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhu, style name Zhongju, was a man of Jinning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhu, style Zhongju, was from Jinning.

sentences.zh: 其父為吏，從征江南，調饒州安仁縣典史，又為杭州鈔庫副使。

translations.literal: His father was a clerk who followed the campaign south of the Yangtze, was transferred to be record-keeper of Anren County in Raozhou, and later became deputy controller of the Hangzhou paper-money vault.
translations.idiomatic: His father was a clerk who followed the southern campaigns, became record-keeper of Anren in Raozhou, then deputy of Hangzhou's paper-money vault.

sentences.zh: 翥少時，負其才雋，豪放不羈，好蹴鞠，喜音樂，不以家業屑其意，其父以為憂。

translations.literal: When young Zhu prized his brilliant talent, was bold and unrestrained, loved kickball and delighted in music, and did not regard the family trade as worth a thought; his father worried over this.
translations.idiomatic: Young Zhu was brilliant and wild, loving kickball and music, caring nothing for the family trade—his father despaired.

sentences.zh: 翥一旦翻然改曰：「大人勿憂，今請易業矣。」

translations.literal: One day Zhu turned about and said: "Father, do not worry—I now ask to change my course."
translations.idiomatic: One day he turned and said, "Father, do not worry. I shall change my trade."

sentences.zh: 乃謝客，閉門讀書，晝夜不暫輟，因受業於李存先生。

translations.literal: Thereupon he dismissed visitors, shut his door and read books day and night without pause, and received instruction from Master Li Cun.
translations.idiomatic: He shut out guests, read night and day without pause, and studied under Master Li Cun.

sentences.zh: 存家安仁，江東大儒也，其學傳於陸九淵氏，翥從之遊，道德性命之說，多所研究。

translations.literal: Li's family was in Anren; he was a great scholar of Jiangdong, his learning transmitted from the school of Lu Jiuyuan. Zhu traveled with him and studied much in the doctrines of moral nature and fate.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cun of Anren was a great scholar of the southeast, heir to Lu Jiuyuan's school. Zhu studied with him, probing doctrines of nature and moral principle.

sentences.zh: 未幾，留杭，又從仇遠先生學。

translations.literal: Before long he stayed at Hangzhou and studied further under Master Qiu Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he stayed on in Hangzhou and studied under Master Qiu Yuan.

sentences.zh: 遠於詩最高，翥學之，盡得其音​​律之奧，於是翥遂以詩文知名一時。

translations.literal: Yuan excelled most in poetry; Zhu studied with him and fully grasped the subtlety of tone and rhythm; thus Zhu soon became renowned in his age for poetry and prose.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Yuan mastered poetry; Zhu learned from him every secret of meter and tune, and soon his verse and prose were famous throughout the land.

sentences.zh: 已而薄遊維揚，居久之，學者及門甚眾。

translations.literal: Afterward he traveled lightly to Weiyang and dwelt there long; scholars who came to his gate were very many.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled to Yangzhou and stayed long; scholars thronged his door.

sentences.zh: 至元末，同郡傅巖起居中書，薦翥隱逸。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhiyuan era, his fellow townsman Fu Yan, Attendant of the Central Secretariat, recommended Zhu as a secluded scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Zhiyuan era, fellow townsman Fu Yan of the Secretariat recommended Zhu as a recluse scholar.

sentences.zh: 至正初，召為國子助教，分教上都生。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhizheng he was summoned as Junior Instructor of the National University, assigned to teach students at Shangdu.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhizheng's opening he was summoned as National University junior instructor to teach students at Shangdu.

sentences.zh: 尋退居淮東。

translations.literal: Soon he withdrew to dwell in eastern Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he retired to east Huai.

sentences.zh: 會朝廷修遼、金、宋三史，起為翰林國史院編修官。

translations.literal: When the court undertook to compile the histories of Liao, Jin, and Song, he was appointed Compiler of the Hanlin National History Institute.
translations.idiomatic: When the court compiled the Liao, Jin, and Song histories, he was raised as Hanlin national history compiler.

sentences.zh: 史成，歷應奉、修撰，遷太常博士，升禮儀院判官，又遷翰林，歷直學士、侍講學士，乃以侍讀兼祭酒。

translations.literal: When the histories were completed he served successively as Imperial Composer and Revising Compiler, was transferred to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, promoted to Vice Director of the Ritual Court, again transferred to Hanlin, passed through Academician-in-Attendance and Lecturing Academician, and finally became Lecturing Academician concurrently Rector.
translations.idiomatic: After the histories were done he rose through composer and reviser posts to erudite of the Sacrifices Court, ritual vice director, then Hanlin—a progression through attending and lecturing academician until he held both lecturing academician and rector.

sentences.zh: 翥勤於誘掖後進，絕去崖岸，不徒以師道自尊，用是學者樂親炙之。

translations.literal: Zhu was diligent in guiding and drawing on juniors, utterly setting aside aloof barriers, not merely holding himself lofty in the teacher's dignity; hence scholars delighted to draw near him.
translations.idiomatic: He worked hard to lift juniors, shed all pretense of distance, and never masked himself in the teacher's dignity—scholars loved to draw near his warmth.

sentences.zh: 有以經義請問者，必歷舉眾說，為之折衷，論辯之際，雜以談笑，無不厭其所得而後已。

translations.literal: When anyone asked about the meaning of the classics he would always traverse the various schools of opinion and reconcile them; amid discussion and debate he would mix in jest and banter, never tiring until his hearer was satisfied with what he had gained.
translations.idiomatic: On classical questions he weighed every school and reconciled them; debate blended with laughter until the questioner was satisfied.

sentences.zh: 嘗奉旨詣中書，集議時政，眾論蜂起，翥獨默然。

translations.literal: Once, by imperial command, he went to the Central Secretariat to assemble and deliberate current policy; opinions swarmed like bees, but Zhu alone was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Once ordered to the Secretariat to debate current policy, he alone stayed silent while others buzzed.

sentences.zh: 丞相搠思監曰：「張先生平日好論事，今一語不出何耶？」

translations.literal: Chancellor Shisim Jian said: "Master Zhang is ordinarily fond of discussing affairs—why not a single word today?"
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Shisim Jian said, "Master Zhang always has views—why not one word today?"

sentences.zh: 翥對曰：「諸人之議，皆是也。

translations.literal: Zhu replied: "The gentlemen's proposals are all right.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu replied, "The gentlemen's proposals are all right.

sentences.zh: 但事勢有緩急，施行有先後，在丞相所決耳。」

translations.literal: Only that affairs have urgency and ease, and execution has order of before and after—it rests with the Chancellor to decide."
translations.idiomatic: Only that affairs have their urgency and their season, and execution its order—all that rests with the chancellor."

sentences.zh: 搠思監善之。

translations.literal: Shisim Jian approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: Shisim Jian approved.

sentences.zh: 明日，除集賢學士，俄以翰林學士承旨致仕，階榮祿大夫。

translations.literal: The next day he was appointed Academic Scholar of the Collected Treasures, and soon retired as Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts, rank Glory and Blessing Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: Next day he was made Collected Treasures academician; soon he retired as Hanlin recipient of edicts at the rank of Glory and Blessing Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 孛羅帖木兒之入京師也，命翥草詔，削奪擴廓帖木兒官爵，且發兵討之，翥毅然不從。

translations.literal: When Boluo Temur entered the capital he ordered Zhu to draft an edict stripping Kozha Temur of office and rank and moreover dispatching troops to punish him; Zhu firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: When Boluo Temur entered the capital he ordered Zhu to draft an edict stripping Kozha Temur and sending troops against him; Zhu refused flatly.

sentences.zh: 左右或勸之，翥曰：「吾臂可斷，筆不能操也。」

translations.literal: Those beside him sometimes urged him; Zhu said: "My arm may be cut off, but the brush I cannot hold."
translations.idiomatic: Some urged him; he said, "You may sever my arm, but I will not take up the brush."

sentences.zh: 天子知其意不可奪，乃命他學士為之。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven knew his intent could not be swayed and then ordered another academician to do it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw his resolve could not be bent and had another academician write it.

sentences.zh: 孛羅帖木兒雖知之，亦不以為怨也。

translations.literal: Though Boluo Temur knew of this, he did not regard it as a grievance.
translations.idiomatic: Boluo Temur knew and bore no grudge.

sentences.zh: 及孛羅帖木兒既誅，詔乃以翥為河南行省平章政事，仍翰林學士承旨致仕，給全俸終其身。

translations.literal: After Boluo Temur was executed, an edict then appointed Zhu Grand Councillor of the Henan Branch Secretariat, still retiring as Hanlin Recipient of Edicts, granting full salary for life.
translations.idiomatic: After Boluo Temur's execution, Zhu was named grand councillor of Henan while remaining retired Hanlin recipient of edicts with full salary for life.

sentences.zh: 二十八年三月卒，年八十二。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twenty-eighth year he died, aged eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third month of year 28, aged eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 翥長於詩，其近體、長短句尤工。

translations.literal: Zhu excelled in poetry; regulated verse and ci lyrics were especially masterful.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled in poetry; regulated verse and ci were his especial mastery.

sentences.zh: 文不如詩，而每以文自負。

translations.literal: His prose was not the equal of his poetry, yet he often took pride in his prose.
translations.idiomatic: His prose did not equal his verse, yet he prized it more.

sentences.zh: 常語人曰：「吾於文已化矣，蓋吾未嘗構思，特任意屬筆而已。」

translations.literal: He often told people: "In prose I have already been transformed—for I never compose in thought; I merely let the brush follow inclination."
translations.idiomatic: He would say, "My prose writes itself—I never plan it; the brush simply follows impulse."

sentences.zh: 它日，翰林學士沙剌班示以所為文，請易置數字，苦思者移時，終不就。

translations.literal: Another day Academician Shala Ban showed him a piece he had written and asked him to shift a few characters; Zhu strained in thought for a long interval but in the end could not do it.
translations.idiomatic: Once Hanlin academician Shala Ban showed him a draft and asked him to change a few words; Zhu brooded a long while and could not.

sentences.zh: 沙剌班曰：「先生於文，豈猶未化耶，何思之苦也？」

translations.literal: Shala Ban said: "Master, in prose have you not yet been transformed? Why such bitter thinking?"
translations.idiomatic: Shala Ban said, "Master, is prose still unmastered for you? Why such agony?"

sentences.zh: 翥因相視大笑。

translations.literal: Zhu thereupon looked at each other with him and laughed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: They looked at each other and laughed.

sentences.zh: 蓋翥平日善諧謔，出談吐語，輒令人失笑，一座盡傾，入其室，藹然春風中也。

translations.literal: For Zhu was ordinarily skilled in wit and raillery; whenever he spoke in conversation his words would make people lose composure in laughter—the whole gathering would be won over; entering his chamber was like a mild spring breeze.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu loved raillery; a word from him could overturn a table with laughter. His chamber breathed spring.

sentences.zh: 所為詩文甚多。

translations.literal: What he wrote in poetry and prose was very abundant.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry and prose were voluminous.

sentences.zh: 無丈夫子。

translations.literal: He had no son.
translations.idiomatic: He had no sons.

sentences.zh: 及死，國遂亡，以故其遺稿不傳。

translations.literal: When he died the state soon perished; for this reason his remaining drafts were not transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: He died; the dynasty soon followed; his papers did not circulate.

sentences.zh: 其傳者，有律詩、樂府，僅三卷。

translations.literal: What was transmitted had regulated poems and yuefu lyrics in only three scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: What survives—regulated verse and yuefu—fills only three scrolls.

sentences.zh: 翥嘗集兵興以來死節死事之人為書，曰《忠義錄》，識者韙之。

translations.literal: Zhu once compiled a book of those who died for principle and died for duty since soldiers first rose in arms, titled Record of Loyalty and Righteousness; men of judgment approved it.
translations.idiomatic: He once compiled a Record of Loyal and Righteous Acts listing men who died for principle or duty since the wars began; discerning readers approved.
